questions.stem: A cash-basis individual taxpayer owns 55% of Stone, a C corporation. Stone uses the accrual method of accounting and owes the taxpayer $4,500 for rent incurred during Year 1. In Year 2, one-half of this expense was paid and reported as income by the taxpayer. What amount of this expense may Stone deduct for Year 2?
questions.explanation:
Owner-employees who own 50% or more of a corporation, along with the corporation itself, are considered related parties. According to these rules, an accrual-method corporation cannot deduct an expense for a liability owed to a cash-basis related owner-employee until that related party recognizes the income.

In this scenario, Stone and the taxpayer are related parties because the taxpayer owns 55% of Stone. Under the tax rules, Stone's use of the accrual method of accounting for this transaction is ignored. Because the taxpayer reported the $2,250 payment (1/2 of the $4,500) as income in Year 2, Stone is required to deduct the matching amount of $2,250 in Year 2.
questions.explanationJa: 50%以上を所有する株主兼従業員と法人は関連当事者とされ、発生主義の法人は現金主義の関連当事者に対する債務を、相手方が所得を認識するまで損金算入できない。納税者はStoneの55%を所有するため関連当事者に該当し、Stoneの発生主義は無視される。Year 2に納税者が$4,500の半分である$2,250を受け取って所得計上したので、Stoneが同年に控除できるのも対応する$2,250である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.1

questions.stem: If a corporation incurs $8,000 of organizational costs, the costs

choices.label: A
choices.text: May be deducted in full in the year in which these costs are incurred even if paid in later years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: May be deducted only in the year in which these costs are paid.

choices.label: C
choices.text: May be amortized over a period of not less than 180 months even if these costs are capitalized on the company's books.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Are nondeductible capital expenditures.

questions.explanation: In this scenario, the corporation's organizational costs total $8,000. $5,000 of the costs are immediately deductible with the remaining $3,000 amortized over 180 months starting in the month that business operations begin
questions.explanationJa: 設立費用は、うち$5,000を即時に控除でき、残額は事業開始月から180か月以上で償却する。本問では$8,000のうち$5,000を即時控除し、残りの$3,000を180か月で償却する。したがって、帳簿上資産計上していても税務上は180か月以上で償却できるという記述が正しい。全額を発生年や支払年に控除できるわけではなく、控除不能な資本的支出でもない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.2

questions.stem: Kari Corp., a manufacturing company, was organized on January 2, Year 3. Its Year 3 federal taxable income was $400,000 and its federal income tax was $100,000. What is the maximum amount of accumulated taxable income that may be subject to the accumulated earnings tax for Year 3 if Kari takes only the minimum accumulated earnings credit?
questions.explanation:
The accumulated earnings tax (AET) is an additional tax imposed on corporations to penalize them for accumulatingretained earningsbeyond their reasonable needs for expansion, retirement of debt, and working capital. The penalty exists to encourage corporations to pay dividends to shareholders, who will then pay more in taxes when they are taxed at the shareholder level.

The AET is imposed on a corporation's accumulated taxable income. The basic calculation of accumulated taxable income is federal taxable income less these three amounts:

An accumulated earnings credit of $250,000 (or $150,000 for a personal service corporation)

Any dividends actually paid to shareholders or dividends the shareholders consented to be taxed on for the taxable year

Any sum retained to pay federal income taxes owed for the tax year

A corporation that pays the personal holding company tax for any taxable year is not also subject to the AET for that same taxable year.

In this scenario, Kari Corp.'s accumulated taxable income is $50,000, calculated as follows:

Federal taxable income | $400,000
Less:
Accumulated earnings credit | (250,000)
Dividends paid to shareholders | 0
Amount retained to pay Year 3 taxes | (100,000)
Accumulated taxable income subject to AET | $50,000
questions.explanationJa: 留保金課税（AET）は、事業上の合理的な必要を超えて利益を内部留保する法人に課される追加税であり、課税対象は累積課税所得である。累積課税所得は、課税所得から留保金控除（通常$250,000、人的役務法人は$150,000）、実際に支払った配当、当期の連邦法人税を差し引いて求める。Kari Corp.は$400,000 − $250,000 − 配当$0 − 法人税$100,000 = $50,000となり、これがAETの対象となる最大額である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.3

questions.stem: A parent C corporation and its subsidiary are both accrual basis taxpayers and elected to file a consolidated tax return in Year 1. During the year, the parent received $50,000 in dividends from the subsidiary. For Year 1, the parent had taxable income of $600,000 before the dividends received deduction. The subsidiary reported a $100,000 loss, which included $20,000 of intercompany gains. What amount of taxable income should be reported on the consolidated tax return in Year 1?
questions.explanation:
When a parent C corporation and its subsidiary file a consolidated tax return, the entities are treated as a single taxpayer. The consolidated return reports the combined incomes (losses) adjusted for certain intercompany transactions (gains/losses, dividends). Because intercompany transactions are between related parties (not at arm's length), they are considered self-dealing (selling to and paying yourself).

Accordingly, most intercompany transactions are excluded from the calculation of consolidated taxable income. For example, an intercompany gain from a sale of property is deferred and therefore excluded from consolidated income until the recipient disposes of the property to a third party ("$450,000"). Dividends received from the parent or subsidiary are eliminated, and no offsetting dividends received deduction is allowed ("$480,000").

In this scenario, the parent's $600,000 taxable income (before the dividends received deduction) is reduced for the $50,000 dividends received from the subsidiary. Because the subsidiary's $100,000 loss included $20,000 intercompany gains, the loss is increased to $120,000 when the gains are eliminated. The consolidated taxable income is $430,000 as shown below.

Parent's income | $600,000
Eliminate dividends received | (50,000)
Parent's adjusted income |  | $550,000
Subsidiary's loss | ($100,000)
Eliminate intercompany gain | (20,000)
Subsidiary's adjusted loss |  | (120,000)
Consolidated taxable income |  | $430,000
questions.explanationJa: 連結納税では親会社と子会社を単一の納税者として扱い、グループ内取引の損益や配当は消去する。グループ内の資産売却益は外部に売却されるまで繰り延べられ、子会社からの受取配当は消去されるため受取配当控除も認められない。親会社の$600,000から受取配当$50,000を消去して$550,000、子会社の損失$100,000にはグループ内利益$20,000が含まれるので消去して損失$120,000とする。連結課税所得は$550,000 − $120,000 = $430,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.4

questions.stem: A corporation that has both preferred and common stock has a deficit in accumulated earnings and profits at the beginning of the year. The current earnings and profits is $25,000. The corporation makes a dividend distribution of $20,000 to the preferred shareholders and $10,000 to the common shareholders. How will the preferred and common shareholders report these distributions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Preferred - $20,000 dividend income; Common - $10,000 dividend income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Preferred - $20,000 dividend income; Common - $5,000 dividend income, $5,000 return of capital.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Preferred - $15,000 dividend income; Common - $10,000 dividend income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Preferred - $20,000 return of capital; Common - $10,000 return of capital.

questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the corporation's positive E&P is $25,000; therefore, dividend income is limited to that amount. Because preferred shareholders are paid first, they will report their entire $20,000 distribution as dividend income ("Preferred - $15,000 dividend income; Common - $10,000 dividend income."). The common shareholders will report $5,000 as dividend income and $5,000 as return of capital, as shown below.

Positive E&P | $25,000
Preferred shareholders' $20,000 distribution | (20,000)
E&P balance | $5,000
Common shareholders' $10,000 distribution | (5,000)*
E&P balance | $0
*The remaining $5,000 distribution ($10,000 − $5,000) is a nontaxable return of capital.:
questions.explanationJa: 当期E&Pは$25,000なので、配当所得となるのはこの額までである。優先株主に先に分配されるため、優先株主は$20,000全額を配当所得として報告する。残るE&Pは$5,000で、普通株主への$10,000のうち$5,000が配当所得、残り$5,000が非課税の資本の払戻しとなる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.5

questions.stem: A corporation had $10,000 of earnings and profits (E&P) for the current year and accumulated negative E&P of $100,000. It paid a cash distribution of $30,000. What amount represents the taxable dividend to the shareholder for that year?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the corporation had positive CEP of $10,000 and negative AEP of $100,000. Because E&P amounts are not netted, $10,000 of the distribution represents the taxable dividend. The remaining $20,000 ($30,000 − $10,000) is a nontaxable return of capital
questions.explanationJa: 当期E&Pが$10,000のプラスで累積E&Pが$100,000のマイナスの場合、両者は相殺しない。そのため当期E&Pの$10,000までが課税配当となる。$30,000の分配のうち残り$20,000（$30,000 − $10,000）は非課税の資本の払戻しである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.6

questions.stem: A C corporation must use the accrual method of accounting if the business

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sells retail goods and had average sales for the past three years of more than $15 million.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Is a service company and had $20 million in sales for the past three years.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Manufactures products and had average sales for the past three years of more than $35 million.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Is a personal service corporation with over $40 million in sales on average for the past three years.

questions.explanation:
C corporations are generally prohibited from using the cash method because it does not clearly reflect income for the tax year. However, there are exceptions for C corporations and partnerships with a C corporation partner if the C corporation is any of the following:

a small business defined as having average annual gross receipts for the preceding three years that are not greater than an inflation-adjusted amount ($27 million), known as the gross receipts test ("Sells retail goods and had average sales for the past three years of…" / "Is a service company and had $20 million in sales for the past three…")

a farming business

a personal service corporation (PSC) ("Is a personal service corporation with over $40 million in sales on a…")
questions.explanationJa: C法人は原則として現金主義を使えず、発生主義が求められる。例外は、過去3年平均の総収入がインフレ調整後の基準額（$27 million）以下の小規模事業者、農業事業、人的役務法人（PSC）である。過去3年平均の売上が$35 millionを超える製造業者はいずれの例外にも当たらないため、発生主義を用いなければならない。売上$20 millionのサービス会社は総収入基準を満たし、PSCは売上規模にかかわらず例外の対象となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.7

questions.stem:
Lake Corp., an accrual-basis calendar year corporation, had the following Year 4 receipts:

Year 5 advance rental payments where the lease ends in Year 6: $125,000
Lease cancellation payment from a 5-year lease tenant: 50,000

Lake had no restrictions on the use of the advance rental payments and renders no services. What amount of income should Lake report on its Year 4 tax return?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Lake Corp. reports taxable income for Year 4 of $175,000, which includes the $125,000 advance rental payments and the $50,000 lease cancellation payment.

Note 1: The advance payment is a temporary tax/book difference on Schedule M-1 that will reverse over time when the revenue is reported on the books when earned.

Note 2:For accrual basis taxpayers, revenue generally is recognized for tax purposes at the earlier of when it is earned or received. Advance payments received for rent and lease cancellation are taxable when received.
questions.explanationJa: 発生主義の納税者でも、税務上の収益は稼得時と受領時のいずれか早い時点で認識する。前受賃料と賃貸借解約金は受領時に課税される。したがってLake Corp.はYear 4に、前受賃料$125,000と解約金$50,000の合計$175,000を所得として報告する。前受賃料は帳簿上は稼得時に収益計上されるため、Schedule M-1上の一時差異となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.8

questions.stem: Andi Corp. issued $1,000,000 face amount of bonds in Year 5 and established a sinking fund to pay the debt at maturity. The bondholders appointed an independent trustee to invest the sinking fund contributions and to administer the trust. In Year 10, the sinking fund earned $60,000 in interest on bank deposits and $8,000 in net long-term capital gains. All of the trust income is accumulated with Andi's periodic contributions so that the aggregate amount will be sufficient to pay the bonds when they mature. What amount of trust income was taxable to Andi in Year 10?
questions.explanation:
Corporations transfer money to bond sinking funds to invest and generate earnings to pay the bond obligations. Sinking funds may be trusts managed by trustees. A sinking fund trust is not a separate taxpayer because the grantor corporation is also its beneficiary. Instead, the trust is an asset of the corporation. Trust income (interest, capital gains) is taxable to the corporation when it is earned.

In this case, Andi Corp.'s sinking fund trust earned $68,000 in Year 10 ($60,000 interest income + $8,000 capital gains); therefore, this income was taxable to Andi in Year 10
questions.explanationJa: 社債の減債基金が受託者の管理する信託であっても、設定者である法人自身が受益者であるため、信託は独立した納税者とはならず法人の資産として扱われる。そのため信託の利息や譲渡益は、稼得した時点で法人に課税される。Andi Corp.の減債基金はYear 10に利息$60,000と長期譲渡益$8,000の合計$68,000を稼得しており、その全額がAndiの課税所得となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.9

questions.stem: The personal holding company income test requires the company's income from passive sources for a given taxable year to be at least

choices.label: A
choices.text: 30% of undistributed personal holding company income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 50% of taxable income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 60% of adjusted ordinary gross income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 80% of ordinary gross income.

questions.explanation:
The personal holding company (PHC) tax was created to discourage the sheltering of certain types of passive income in corporations. This sheltering generally occurs when individuals in high tax brackets establish corporations to hold their personal investments so they can benefit from lower corporate tax rates on the income.

The PHC tax applies in any tax year in which a corporation meets both of the following tests:

Passive income test: 60% of the corporation's adjusted ordinary gross income comes from passive sources (dividends, interest, rent, royalties).

Stock ownership test: Five or fewer individuals own more than 50% of the corporation's stock.

The tax applies to the corporation's undistributed PHC income ("30% of undistributed personal holding company income."). Undistributed PHC income is based on the corporation's taxable income with adjustments as listed on Schedule PH of Form 1120. The tax can be reduced or eliminated by dividend distribution, which results in the shareholders' paying taxes on those dividends.
questions.explanationJa: 同族持株会社（PHC）税は、高税率の個人が法人を使って受動的所得を蓄える行為を抑止するための税である。PHC税は、調整後通常総所得の60%以上が受動的所得（配当、利子、賃料、ロイヤルティ）であるという所得基準と、5人以下の個人が株式の50%超を所有するという株式所有基準の両方を満たす年に課される。未分配PHC所得は課税対象そのものであり、所得基準の判定指標ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.10

questions.stem:
Pierce Corp., an accrual basis, calendar-year C corporation, had the following Year 7 receipts:

Year 8 advance rental payments for which the rental period ends in Year 9: $250,000
Advance payment for computer services to be rendered for 10 months beginning December 1, Year 7: 100,000

Pierce had no restrictions on the use of the advance rental payments and rendered no services in connection with the rental income. Where permissible, Pierce elects to defer revenue. What amount of gross income should Pierce report on its Year 7 tax return?
questions.explanation:
Advance payments received generally are recognized as taxable revenue in the year received ("$0"). Taxpayers may elect to include part of advance payments for goods and services (computer services) that are earned in the year received; the remainder is reported in the following year. However, this election excludes advance rental and insurance premium payments received.

In this scenario, Pierce Corp. elects to defer any permissible advance payments such as the computer services. Accordingly, only 1 month's income is taxable in Year 7 with the remaining 9 months' income taxable in Year 8. No deferral is allowed for advance rental payments. Pierce reports $260,000 as taxable income on its Year 7 tax return, as shown below.

Advance rental payments: $250,000
Prorated computer services ($100,000 / 10 months = $10,000 per month): 10,000
Total income reported in Year 7: $260,000
questions.explanationJa: 前受金は原則として受領年に課税されるが、商品やサービスの前受金については、受領年に稼得した部分だけを計上し残りを翌年に繰り延べる選択ができる。ただし前受賃料と保険料はこの繰延べの対象外である。Pierce Corp.は前受賃料$250,000を全額Year 7に計上し、コンピューターサービス代$100,000は月$10,000（$100,000 ÷ 10か月）のうち12月の1か月分$10,000のみを計上する。Year 7の総所得は$250,000 + $10,000 = $260,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.11

questions.stem: Jagdon Corp.'s book income was $150,000 for the current year, including interest income from municipal bonds of $5,000 and excess capital losses over capital gains of $10,000. Federal income tax expense of $50,000 was also included in Jagdon's books. What amount represents Jagdon's taxable income for the current year?
questions.explanation:
Jagdon Corp.'s book income of $150,000 is reconciled to $205,000 of taxable income as follows:

Book income: $150,000
+ Expenses deducted on books but not on tax return: Excess capital losses / 10,000
Federal income taxes: 50,000
− Income reported on books but not on tax return: Municipal bond interest / (5,000)
Taxable income: $205,000
questions.explanationJa: 帳簿利益から課税所得を求めるには、帳簿で費用計上したが税務上は損金とならない項目を加算し、帳簿で収益計上したが課税されない項目を減算する。資本損失の超過額$10,000と連邦法人税$50,000は加算し、地方債利息$5,000は減算する。課税所得は$150,000 + $10,000 + $50,000 − $5,000 = $205,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.12

questions.stem:
A C corporation distributed the following assets to its shareholders as part of a complete liquidation:

Basis | FMV
Unimproved land | $200,000 | $125,000
Inventory | 80,000 | 95,000

What amount of ordinary income or loss did the corporation recognize as a result of the distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No ordinary income or loss.

choices.label: B
choices.text: $15,000 ordinary income

choices.label: C
choices.text: $60,000 ordinary loss.

choices.label: D
choices.text: $75,000 ordinary loss.

questions.explanation:
In general, when a corporation distributes property to a shareholder in a complete liquidation, the corporation reports gains and losses as if the assets were sold to the shareholder at FMV. The corporation recognizes a gain or loss for the difference between the property's FMV (less any liability assumed by the shareholder) on the date of distribution and property's adjusted basis ("No ordinary income or loss.").

The type of recognized gain or loss (capital or ordinary) depends on the nature of the asset distributed.

Capital assets generate capital gains and losses

Ordinary income-producing assets (inventory) result in ordinary income or loss

Section 1231 assets (equipment) are subject to ordinary income depreciation recapture with the remaining balance classified as a capital gain or an ordinary loss

In this scenario, the inventory is the only ordinary income-producing asset. Accordingly, the corporation recognizes ordinary income of $15,000 ($95,000 FMV − $80,000 adjusted basis).
questions.explanationJa: 完全清算で資産を分配した法人は、資産を株主に時価で売却したものとして、時価と調整後簿価の差額を損益として認識する。損益の性質は資産の種類で決まり、資本資産からは譲渡損益、棚卸資産からは通常所得・損失が生じる。本問で通常所得を生む資産は棚卸資産だけであり、通常所得は$95,000 − $80,000 = $15,000となる。土地の損失は資本損失であり、通常損失には含めない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.13

questions.stem:
Porter, the sole shareholder of Preston Corp., transferred property to the corporation as a contribution to capital. Two years later, Corley transferred property to the corporation in exchange for a 10% interest in corporate stock. The property transferred was valued as follows:

Porter's transfer | Corley's transfer
Basis | $50,000 | $250,000
Fair market value | $250,000 | $500,000

What amount represents the corporation's basis in the property received?
questions.explanation:
When a shareholder contributes property in exchange for stock in a corporation, the transfer may be taxable or nontaxable, depending on the percentage of ownership control. The transfer is nontaxable if 80% or more of the corporate stock is acquired, with cash or property, by the shareholders purchasing the stock.

If the transfer is nontaxable, the shareholder's adjusted tax basis for the contributed property carries over to the corporation. However, if the 80% threshold is not met, the transfer is taxable to the shareholder (reported as a sale). The property's FMV on the date of the contribution is used to value the stock. Because the transfer is taxable, the corporation values the property at FMV.

When determining whether the 80% threshold requirement is met, transfers are aggregated only if those transfers are part of a group plan to acquire stock. Otherwise, each transfer must meet the 80% requirement individually.

In this scenario, there are two separate stock transfers.

Porter's transfer of property was for 100% (sole shareholder) of the stock. Because the 80% ownership test is met, the transfer is nontaxable and Porter's $50,000 adjusted tax basis in the property carries over to the corporation.

Corley's transfer was for 10% ownership, thus failing the 80% ownership test. This transfer is taxable and the corporation takes on the $500,000 FMV in Corley's property.

Therefore, the corporation's total basis in all property is $550,000 ($50,000 + $500,000).
questions.explanationJa: 株式と引換えの資産拠出は、拠出者が拠出直後に80%以上の支配を得れば非課税となり、拠出者の調整後簿価が法人に引き継がれる。80%に満たなければ拠出者にとって課税取引となり、法人は資産を時価で受け入れる。80%判定は一体の計画による拠出でない限り別々に行う。Porterの拠出は唯一の株主によるもので非課税となり簿価$50,000を引き継ぎ、Corleyの拠出は10%取得で課税されるため時価$500,000となり、合計$550,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.14

questions.stem: Hubert Hanson owns 40% of Calico Corp.'s outstanding shares; Hanson's spouse owns 20%. In a qualifying stock redemption Calico exchanges $100,000 cash for half of Hubert Hanson's stock. At the time of the redemption, Hubert's adjusted basis in all of his Calico stock was $300,000. Additionally, just prior to the redemption, Calico Corp. had accumulated earnings and profits (E&P) of ($20,000) and current E&P of $25,000. What amount of income, gain or loss will Hanson recognize as a result of the redemption?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No income, gain or loss will be recognized

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dividend income of $25,000

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capital loss of $50,000

choices.label: D
choices.text: Capital gain of $25,000

questions.explanation: Including the stock owned by Hubert's wife, which is considered to be indirectly owned by Hubert, Hanson owns 60% of Calico. Although the sale of half of his interest, which has a basis of $150,000 (i.e., 50% × $300,000), for $100,000 results in a loss of $50,000. However, when a shareholder directly or indirectly owns more than 50% at the time of the redemption, losses are disallowed.
questions.explanationJa: 配偶者が所有する株式はHubertが間接的に所有するものとみなされるため、HansonのCalico株式の持分は合計60%となる。保有株式の半分（簿価$300,000 × 50% = $150,000）を$100,000で償還したことで$50,000の損失が生じる。しかし償還時に直接・間接に50%超を所有する株主の損失は認められないため、Hansonが認識する所得・利得・損失はない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.15

questions.stem: On January 1, Year 9, Kee Corp., a C corporation, had a $50,000 deficit in earnings and profits. For Year 9, Kee had current earnings and profits of $10,000 and made a $30,000 cash distribution to its stockholders. What amount of the distribution is taxable as dividend income to Kee's stockholders?
questions.explanation:
Dividends are made from positive corporate earnings and profits (E&P).

E&P has two parts that are addressed separately: current E&P (CEP) and accumulated E&P (AEP).

CEP is equal to adjusted current year income (loss) (may be positive or a deficit).

Undistributed positive CEP becomes AEP available for future distributions.

Deficit CEP reduces AEP and may create deficit AEP.

When CEP is positive, distributions are dividends up to positive CEP and then up to any positive AEP.

Dividends are taxable income to shareholders. Distributions in excess of E&P are return of capital (ROC) distributions that reduce a recipient shareholder's stock basis, but not below zero. Any ROC distribution amount in excess of a shareholder's stock basis is taxable capital gain to the shareholder.

In this scenario, Kee Corp. had $10,000 in positive CEP and deficit AEP. Thus, $10,000 of the $30,000 distribution is taxable as dividend income to Kee's stockholders ("$0"). The remaining $20,000 is an ROC distribution
questions.explanationJa: 配当は法人のプラスのE&Pから行われ、当期E&Pと累積E&Pは別々に扱う。当期E&Pがプラスなら、分配はまず当期E&Pの範囲で配当となり、次にプラスの累積E&Pがあればその範囲で配当となる。Kee Corp.は当期E&Pが$10,000で累積E&Pは$50,000の赤字なので、$30,000の分配のうち$10,000が配当所得となる。残り$20,000は資本の払戻しとして株式の簿価を減らす。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.16

questions.stem: Which of the following items should be included on the Schedule M-1, Reconciliation of Income (Loss) per Books With Income per Return, of Form 1120, U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return, to reconcile book income to taxable income?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cash distributions to shareholders.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Premiums paid on key-person life insurance policy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Corporate bond interest.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ending balance of retained earnings.

questions.explanation:
A corporation reconciles book income to taxable income on Schedule M-1 to account for these differences. There are two types of differences:

Temporary differences result from the same item's being calculated differently for accounting (GAAP) than for tax purposes (different book/tax depreciation methods) in any given reporting year. These differences eventually work themselves out over time.

Permanent differences are items that are income or deductions in the year for either book or taxable income but not both (tax-exempt interest). These differences do not reverse over time.

Temporary and permanent differences are either added to or deducted from book income to determine taxable income. For example, premiums paid on a key-person life insurance policy are an expense for book income but nondeductible for taxable income. Accordingly, they are a permanent difference that should be added back to book income in the Schedule M-1 reconciliation.

("Cash distributions to shareholders." / "Ending balance of retained earnings.") Cash distributions and the ending balance of retained earnings are included on Schedule M-2, Reconciliation of Unappropriated Retained Earnings per Books.

("Corporate bond interest.") Corporate bond interest is included in income for both book and tax purposes. Therefore, there is no reportable difference on Schedule M-1.
questions.explanationJa: Schedule M-1は帳簿利益と課税所得の差異を調整する表であり、差異には将来解消する一時差異と解消しない永久差異がある。役員保険（キーパーソン生命保険）の保険料は、帳簿上は費用だが税務上は損金不算入なので、永久差異として帳簿利益に加算する。現金配当や期末利益剰余金はSchedule M-2で扱う項目である。社債利息は帳簿上も税務上も収益となるため、M-1に差異は生じない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.17

questions.stem: As the result of an IRS audit of a C corporation and its sole shareholder, the IRS agent proposes that a portion of the shareholder's salary is unreasonable. Because the corporation has significant earnings and profits, the agent has determined that the unreasonable portion of the salary is a dividend. Which of the following is correct regarding the impact of the proposed adjustment to both the corporation and its shareholder?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Full disallowance of salary expense, a corresponding increase in nondeductible dividends to the corporation, and no effect on the shareholder since both salaries and dividends are taxable income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Partial disallowance of salary expense, a corresponding increase in nondeductible dividends to the corporation, and reclassification of the shareholder's salary to dividend treatment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Allowance of the full amount as salary expense to the corporation and reclassification of the unreasonable portion of the shareholder's salary to dividend treatment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Partial disallowance of salary expense, a corresponding increase in deductible dividends to the corporation, and no effect on the shareholder's return since both salaries and dividends are taxable income.

questions.explanation:
Transactions between a corporation and its shareholder-employees are subject to scrutiny because they are not at arm's-length and therefore can be manipulated. For example, part of the salary paid to a shareholder-employee may exceed the actual value of the services provided and would result in the understatement of corporate profits. Any portion of a shareholder-employee's salary deemed excessive is disallowed as an expense and reclassified as a dividend (reduction of equity) paid by the corporation and dividend income to the shareholder.

("Full disallowance of salary expense, a corresponding increase in nond…" / "Allowance of the full amount as salary expense to the corporation and…" / "Partial disallowance of salary expense, a corresponding increase in d…") The corporation is allowed a salary deduction for the compensation that represents the value of services performed by the shareholder-employee. If the compensation is deemed unreasonable, a reclassification is made between deductible salary expense and dividends paid (nondeductible). Although the shareholder-employee's total income is the same, the character of income is divided between wages earned and dividend income.
questions.explanationJa: 法人と株主兼従業員の取引は独立当事者間取引ではないため、役員報酬のうち役務の価値を超える部分は過大とされる。過大部分は報酬としての損金算入が否認され、損金不算入の配当として再分類される。株主側では所得総額は変わらないが、所得の性質が給与と配当に分かれる。したがって報酬の一部否認、それに対応する損金不算入の配当の増加、株主の給与の一部の配当への再分類が正しい。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.18

questions.stem: At the beginning of the year, Data, a C corporation, had a $45,000 deficit in accumulated earnings and profits. For the current year, Data reported earnings and profits of $15,000. Data distributed $18,000 to its shareholders during the current year. What amount of the distribution is treated as a taxable dividend?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, Data had $15,000 of positive CEP and a $45,000 AEP deficit. Data's $18,000 distribution is a taxable dividend up to the extent of the $15,000 positive CEP. Because AEP is a deficit, the remaining $3,000 is classified as an ROC distribution.
questions.explanationJa: Dataの当期E&Pは$15,000のプラス、累積E&Pは$45,000の赤字であり、両者は相殺しない。$18,000の分配は、当期E&Pの$15,000までが課税配当となる。累積E&Pが赤字なので、残り$3,000は資本の払戻しとなる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.19

questions.stem: Red Corp. and White, Inc. are calendar-year domestic C corporations. Red owns 80% of White's voting stock. In Year 5, Yellow Corp., a calendar-year S corporation, acquired 95% of the voting stock of Red Corp. Assuming no election has been made concerning consolidated returns in prior years, which of the following corporations may file a consolidated return for Year 5?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Red and White.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Red and Yellow.

choices.label: C
choices.text: White and Yellow.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Red, White, and Yellow.

questions.explanation:
Only domestic C corporations that are members of an affiliated group can file a consolidated return. An affiliated group exists when:

One C corporation (the parent) owns at least 80 percent of the value of another C corporation's outstanding voting stock, and

All other member C corporations are at least 80% owned by the parent and/or other group members.

S corporations are permitted to own stock of a C corporation. Because S corporations are pass-through entities, an S parent corporation (Yellow Corp.) cannot be included as a member of the affiliated group for federal tax purposes.

In this scenario, only Red and White (parent and subsidiary) qualify as an affiliated group that may file a consolidated return. Although Yellow Corp. owns 95% of Red Corp.'s voting stock, Yellow is not a member of the affiliated group because it is an S corporation and therefore ineligible
questions.explanationJa: 連結納税ができるのは、関連グループに属する国内C法人だけである。関連グループは、親会社となるC法人が他のC法人の議決権株式の80%以上を所有し、他のメンバーもすべて親会社や他のメンバーに80%以上所有されている場合に成立する。S法人はパススルー事業体であり、C法人株式を所有できても関連グループのメンバーにはなれない。YellowはRedの95%を所有するがS法人なので除かれ、連結納税ができるのはRedとWhiteだけである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.20

questions.stem:
Brown Corp., a calendar-year taxpayer, was organized and actively began operations on July 1, Year 2, and incurred the following costs:

Legal fees to obtain corporate charter | $ 40,000
Commission paid to underwriter | 25,000
Other stock issue costs | 10,000

Brown elects to amortize its organizational costs. In Year 2, what is the maximum amount Brown may deduct from taxable income as a result of organizational expenses incurred?
questions.explanation:
Organizational costs include state incorporation fees, legal fees, and accounting services incidental to the creation of the corporation. Costs of issuing, printing, and selling stock are not organizational expenses; these costs reduce APIC.

In this scenario, the $40,000 legal fees to obtain a corporate charter are organizational costs, but the $25,000 commission paid and the $10,000 stock issue costs are not. Because Brown Corp. elected to amortize its organizational expenses, $5,000 of the $40,000 is immediately deductible. The $35,000 remaining costs ($40,000 − $5,000) are amortized over 180 months. However, Brown began business on July 1, thus limiting the amortization in Year 2 to $1,167 [($35,000 / 180) × 6 months]. The total amount expensed in Year 2 is $6,167 ($5,000 + $1,167).
questions.explanationJa: 設立費用には州の設立手数料、法務費用、設立に付随する会計費用が含まれるが、株式の発行・印刷・販売費用は含まれず資本剰余金を減らす。したがって定款取得の法務費用$40,000だけが設立費用であり、引受手数料$25,000とその他の株式発行費用$10,000は除く。$40,000のうち$5,000を即時控除し、残り$35,000を180か月で償却するが、7月1日開業なのでYear 2の償却は6か月分の$1,167（$35,000 ÷ 180 × 6）となる。Year 2の控除額は$5,000 + $1,167 = $6,167である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.21

questions.stem:
Jones, Smith, and Black formed a corporation with authorized voting common stock of $200,000. Jones received 20% of the capital stock as payment for $40,000 of legal services performed related to the corporation's organization. Smith and Black transferred property in exchange for stock as follows:

Adjusted basis | FMV | % of stock acquired
Smith | $15,000 | $20,000 | 10%
Black | 90,000 | 140,000 | 70%

What is each shareholder's basis in the stock received?
Jones | Smith | Black
questions.explanation:
The transfer is nontaxable if one or more persons transfer only property and immediately after the exchange own 80% or more of the corporate stock (Smith and Black).

Because services are not property, the FMV of stock received from providing services is reported as taxable compensation, and the shareholder's basis in the stock equals the FMV of the services ("$0 | $15,000 | $90,000" / "$0 | $40,000 | $140,000"). Shares issued for services are excluded when determining the 80% ownership control test.

In general, when the 80% test is met, a shareholder recognizes no gain or loss on the exchange. Because of this nonrecognition, the shareholder's basis in the stock acquired equals their adjusted tax basis (not FMV) in the property transferred. However, the basis may be adjusted for certain items.

In this scenario, Jones performed services in exchange for stock. Therefore, the exchange is taxable and Jones's stock basis equals the $40,000 FMV of the services. Even though Jones's shares are excluded when determining the 80% test, Smith and Black together own 80% (10% + 70%). In addition, Smith and Black contributed property only (no services). As a result, their exchanges are nontaxable and stock basis equals their adjusted tax basis in the contributed property ($15,000 and $90,000, respectively)
questions.explanationJa: 財産のみを拠出した者が拠出直後に合計80%以上を所有すれば、その交換は非課税となる。役務は財産ではないため、役務の対価として受け取った株式の時価は報酬として課税され、株式の簿価は役務の時価となる。また役務提供者の株式は80%判定から除外する。Jonesの株式簿価は役務の時価$40,000であり、SmithとBlackは合計80%（10% + 70%）で支配基準を満たし非課税となるので、株式簿価は拠出財産の調整後簿価である$15,000と$90,000になる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.22

questions.stem:
Press Corp. and Swank Corp. file a consolidated return. The companies had the following items of income and deductions for the current year:

Press Corp. | Swank Corp.
Income from operations | $80,000 | $40,000
Section 1231 loss | (12,000) | 0
Capital gain/(loss) | 4,000 | (3,000)

What is Press and Swank's consolidated taxable income?
questions.explanation:
Press Corp. and Swank Corp.'s items of income and deductions are netted against each other, resulting in the following:

$120,000 - 12,000 + 1,000 (4,000-3,000) = $109,000
questions.explanationJa: 連結納税では、Press Corp.とSwank Corp.の損益項目を合算して相殺する。営業利益は$80,000 + $40,000 = $120,000、Section 1231損失は$12,000、資本損益は$4,000 − $3,000 = $1,000の純利益である。連結課税所得は$120,000 − $12,000 + $1,000 = $109,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.23

questions.stem: A corporation has outstanding 400 shares of common stock owned equally by shareholders A, B, C, and D (100 shares each). The corporation redeems 100 shares as follows: 30 shares from shareholder A, 15 shares from shareholder B, and 55 shares from shareholder C. Shareholder D's ownership remains at 100 shares. Which shareholder(s) qualify for exchange treatment on this redemption?

choices.label: A
choices.text: None.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only shareholder C.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only shareholders A and C.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only shareholders B and C.

questions.explanation:
A stock redemption occurs when a corporation acquires its own stock in exchange for cash (or other property) from a shareholder. The redemption is taxed to the shareholder as either dividend income or as a sale or exchange. Because stock is a capital asset to a shareholder, sales and exchanges result in a capital gain or loss.

The preferential treatment of a redemption as a capital gain, instead of ordinary income (dividend), is permitted if the redemption is substantially disproportionate. For a redemption to be substantially disproportionate:

The shareholder must own < 50% of the outstanding stock after the redemption, and

The shareholder's ownership must be reduced to < 80% of previous ownership of the outstanding stock.

In this scenario, before the redemption each shareholder owned 25% of the corporation (100 shares / 400 total shares). After the redemption, 300 shares (400 − 100 redeemed) are outstanding. Although each shareholder has less than 50% ownership after the redemption, only shareholder C has less than 80% of previous ownership (new ownership now be 15% < 20% [25% previous ownership × 80%]), as shown below.

Shareholder | % before redemption | % ownership after redemption | < 50% after redemption? | < 80% of previous ownership?
A | 25% | (100 − 30 redeemed) / 300 = 23% | Yes | No (23% > 20%)
B | 25% | (100 − 15 redeemed) / 300 = 28% | Yes | No (28% > 20%)
C | 25% | (100 − 55 redeemed) / 300 = 15% | Yes | Yes (15% < 20%)

Accordingly, shareholder C meets the requirements for a substantially disproportionate redemption and treats the redemption as an exchange. Shareholders A and B received dividend treatment to the extent of earnings and profits.
questions.explanationJa: 株式償還は、配当所得とされるか、売却・交換として譲渡損益とされるかのいずれかで課税される。著しく不均衡な償還と認められれば交換として扱われ、その要件は償還後の持分が50%未満であり、かつ償還前持分の80%未満に減少していることである。償還前は各株主25%で、償還後の発行株式は300株となり、基準は25% × 80% = 20%である。Aは70/300 = 23%、Bは85/300 = 28%で基準を上回るが、Cは45/300 = 15%で20%未満となるため、交換扱いを受けるのはCだけである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.24

questions.stem:
Nichol Corp. gave gifts to 15 individuals who were customers of the business. The gifts were not in the nature of advertising. The market values of the gifts were as follows:

5 gifts @ $15 each
9 gifts @ $30 each
1 gift @ $100

What amount is deductible as business gifts?
questions.explanation:
Due to the $25 limit, Nichol Corp. may deduct only $325 as business gifts, as calculated below.

5 gifts @ $15 each | Not limited, 5 × $15 = | $75
9 gifts @ $30 each | Limited, 9 × $25 = | 225
1 gift @ $100 | Limited, 1 × $25 = | 25
15 gifts | Deductible amount | $325
questions.explanationJa: 事業上の贈答品は、受贈者1人あたり$25が控除の上限である。$15の贈答品5個は上限内なので5 × $15 = $75を全額控除できる。$30の贈答品9個は9 × $25 = $225、$100の贈答品1個は$25に制限される。控除額は$75 + $225 + $25 = $325である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.25

questions.stem: Bridge, a C corporation, had $15,000 in accumulated earnings and profits at the beginning of the current year. During the current year, Bridge reported earnings and profits of $10,000 and paid $20,000 in cash distributions to its shareholders in both March and July ($40,000 total distributions for the year). What amount of the July distribution should be classified as dividend income to Bridge's shareholders?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Bridge's $40,000 in total distributions ($20,000 distributed in both March and July) exceeded its $25,000 E&P at year end ($10,000 CEP + $15,000 AEP), requiring E&P to be allocated as follows:

A: Distribution month | March | July | Total
B: Distribution amount | $20,000 | $20,000 | $40,000
C: Percentage of total distributions | 50% | 50% | 100%
D: $10,000 CEP allocated pro rata (B × C) | $5,000 | $5,000 | $10,000
E: Distribution after CEP (B − D) | $15,000 | $15,000 | $30,000
F: $15,000 AEP allocated in order | $15,000 | $0 | $15,000
G: Dividend distribution (D + F) | $20,000 | $5,000 | $25,000
H: ROC distribution (B − G) | $0 | $15,000 | $15,000
questions.explanationJa: 分配総額$40,000が年末時点のE&P$25,000（当期$10,000 + 累積$15,000）を超えるため、E&Pを各分配に配分する必要がある。当期E&P$10,000は分配額に比例して配分するので、3月と7月に$5,000ずつ割り当てる。累積E&P$15,000は分配の時系列順に配分するため、3月の残り$15,000に全額充当され、7月には残らない。7月の分配$20,000のうち配当となるのは当期E&P分の$5,000だけであり、残り$15,000は資本の払戻しである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.26

questions.stem:
Close Corp. distributed cash and a parcel of land in a nonliquidating distribution to its sole shareholder. The following facts apply to this distribution:

Item | Amount
Cash | $50,000
Land:
Fair market value | 30,000
Adjusted basis | 40,000

Based on these facts, what amount of gain or loss should be recognized by Close Corp. as a result of this distribution?

choices.label: B
choices.text: No gain or loss should be recognized.

questions.explanation:
Generally, corporations do not recognize gain or loss when making nonliquidating (current) distributions to shareholders.

However, if appreciated property is distributed, the distribution is treated as a hypothetical sale and the corporation must recognize gain equal to the excess of the property's FMV over adjusted basis. If the property's FMV is less than its basis, no loss is recognized, thus preventing any potential manipulation of gross income. If more than one item is distributed, each item is analyzed separately.

In this scenario, the distribution consists of $50,000 in cash and a land worth $30,000 with a $40,000 adjusted basis.

Cash: Corporations do not realize gain or loss on distributions of cash.

Land: Close Corp. realized a $10,000 loss ($30,000 FMV − $40,000 basis) in distributing the land. The corporation cannot recognize this loss; therefore, no gain or loss should be recognized in the land distribution.

("$60,000 loss.") A $60,000 loss results from adding the $10,000 realized loss on the property distribution to the $50,000 cash distribution. Regardless of the calculation, corporate distribution losses are not recognized.

("$10,000 loss.") Although the corporation realized $10,000 of loss, the loss cannot be recognized.

("$40,000 gain.") A gain of $40,000 equals the $50,000 cash distribution minus the $10,000 loss on the land. This incorrectly treats the two distributions as one, when they must be analyzed separately.
questions.explanationJa: 法人は非清算分配について、原則として損益を認識しない。ただし値上がり資産を分配した場合は売却したものとみなして利得を認識するが、時価が簿価を下回る資産を分配しても損失は認識しない。複数の資産を分配した場合は資産ごとに判定する。現金$50,000からは損益が生じず、土地は$30,000 − $40,000 = $10,000の損失が実現するが認識できないため、認識すべき損益はない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.27

questions.stem: Ames and Roth formed Homerun Inc., a C corporation. Ames contributed several autographed baseballs to Homerun. Ames purchased the baseballs for $500, and they have a total fair market value of $1,000. Roth contributed several autographed baseball bats to Homerun. Roth purchased the bats for $5,000, and they have a fair market value of $7,000. What is Homerun's basis in the contributed bats and balls?
questions.explanation:
When forming a corporation, a transferor (shareholder) contributes property in exchange for stock. The transfer may be taxable or nontaxable, depending on the percentage of ownership control. The transfer is nontaxable if 80% or more of the corporate stock is acquired, with cash or property only, by the shareholder or shareholder group (Ames and Roth).

If the transfer is nontaxable, the shareholder's adjusted tax basis (not FMV) for the contributed property carries over to the corporation ("$0" / "$8,000"). If the shareholder receives cash or other property (boot) in addition to stock from the corporation, the shareholder recognizes a gain equaling the boot received. When this occurs, the carryover basis to the corporation is increased by the shareholder's gain recognized.

In this scenario, Ames and Roth contribute property (baseballs, bats) in exchange for 100% ownership. Because this is a nontaxable exchange and no boot was received by either shareholder, Homerun Inc. assumes the shareholders' carryover basis of $5,500 ($500 for baseballs and $5,000 for bats).
questions.explanationJa: 法人設立時の資産拠出は、拠出者グループが財産のみを拠出して80%以上の株式を取得すれば非課税となる。非課税の場合、法人は拠出者の調整後簿価（時価ではない）を引き継ぎ、拠出者が株式以外の現金等（ブート）を受け取ったときだけ、認識した利得の分だけ引継ぎ簿価が増える。AmesとRothは財産を拠出して100%を所有し、ブートも受け取っていない。Homerun Inc.の簿価はボール$500とバット$5,000を合わせた$5,500である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.28

questions.stem: Borasco Corp. owns land with a fair market value of $200,000. Borasco purchased the land 10 years ago for $65,000 and owes a liability of $50,000 as of August 2 of the current year. Alvo Corp. owns 100% of Borasco. Borasco is completely liquidated on August 2 of the current year, according to a plan adopted on June 18 of the current year. As a result, the land is transferred to Alvo in complete cancellation of Borasco's stock. What basis does Alvo have in the land it receives?
questions.explanation:
In a subsidiary liquidation:

the parent and the subsidiary do not recognize gain or loss on property distributions made to the parent,

the parent's basis in the property equals the subsidiary's basis (carryover basis) in the property, and

the parent keeps the subsidiary's tax attributes (NOL, capital loss and charitable contribution carryovers; earnings and profits).

In this scenario, Borasco Corp.'s liquidation is a nontaxable subsidiary liquidation because Borasco is a subsidiary that is more than 80% owned by Alvo Corp. (another corporation). Thus, Alvo's basis in the land it received is the $65,000 carryover basis from Borasco.
questions.explanationJa: 子会社清算では、親会社への資産分配について親会社も子会社も損益を認識しない。親会社の資産の簿価は子会社の簿価を引き継ぎ、NOLの繰越などの税務属性も親会社が引き継ぐ。BorascoはAlvoに80%超（100%）所有される子会社なので、清算は非課税の子会社清算となる。Alvoの土地の簿価はBorascoから引き継ぐ$65,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.29

questions.stem: Brisk Corp. is an accrual-basis, calendar-year C corporation with one individual shareholder. At year end, Brisk had $600,000 accumulated and current earnings and profits as it prepared to make its only dividend distribution for the year to its shareholder. Brisk could distribute either cash of $200,000 or land with an adjusted tax basis of $75,000 and a fair market value of $200,000. How would the taxable incomes of both Brisk and the shareholder change if land were distributed instead of cash?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase in Brisk's taxable income, no change in shareholder's taxable income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No change in Brisk's taxable income, decrease in shareholder's taxable income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No change in Brisk's taxable income, no change in shareholder's taxable income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase in Brisk's taxable income, decrease in shareholder's taxable income.

questions.explanation:
Generally, nonliquidating distributions do not affect corporate taxable income. However, if appreciated property is distributed, corporations must recognize gain in the excess of property FMV over basis because the distribution is treated as a hypothetical sale.

If the distributing corporation has sufficient earnings and profits (E&P), then the distribution is a dividend and shareholders will include the amount of cash or FMV of the property received in taxable income. E&P is sufficient if it is at least equal to the amount of cash and/or FMV of property distributed.

In this scenario, the distribution is a dividend because Brisk Corp.'s $600,000 E&P is greater than the $200,000 cash/FMV property distributed. The shareholder recognizes $200,000 taxable income if either cash or property is distributed. However, if cash is distributed, Brisk recognizes no taxable income, but if land is distributed, Brisk recognizes $125,000 of taxable income ($200,000 FMV − $75,000 basis = $125,000).
questions.explanationJa: 非清算分配は原則として法人の課税所得に影響しないが、値上がり資産を分配した場合は売却とみなし、時価が簿価を超える額の利得を認識する。株主側では、法人のE&Pが十分なら分配は配当となり、現金額または資産の時価を課税所得に含める。BriskのE&P$600,000は分配額$200,000を上回るため、現金でも土地でも株主の課税所得は$200,000で変わらない。土地を分配するとBriskは$200,000 − $75,000 = $125,000の利得を認識し、課税所得が増える。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.30

questions.stem: Parks and Smith formed a corporation by contributing property with FMV of $50,000 (adjusted basis $25,000) and $70,000 cash, respectively, each for a 50% ownership in the newly formed company. What is Parks' basis in the stock acquired if the company is valued at $120,000?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, because Parks and Smith together own 100% of the stock, the control test is met (≥ 80%). Therefore, both transfers are nontaxable. Parks' basis in the stock acquired is $25,000, the same as the adjusted tax basis of the property transferred.
questions.explanationJa: ParksとSmithは合わせて100%の株式を所有するため、80%以上という支配基準を満たし、両者の拠出は非課税となる。非課税の拠出では、取得した株式の簿価は拠出した財産の調整後簿価と同じになる。したがってParksの株式簿価は、拠出した財産の簿価$25,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.31

questions.stem: Which of the following statements most accurately describes the concept of nexus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nexus is the ability of a state to impose taxes on companies that do business in that state but are headquartered in another state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nexus is the ability of a company to do business in a state.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nexus is the need to allocate income among multiple taxing jurisdictions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nexus is a connection between a company and a state that is sufficient for the state to tax the company.

questions.explanation:
In general, an entity is allowed to do business in states other than the state in which it was formed ("Nexus is the ability of a company to do business in a state."). An entity has nexus with another state when it engages in certain significant activities within that other state. When nexus is established, the entity is then subject to the state's sales and income tax requirements and can be sued there.

Activities that create nexus with a state include:

Maintaining a physical presence (warehouse, branch office) in that state

Having employees (regional sales staff) in that state who also work there. Nexus depends on where employees perform services, not where they reside

Selling a significant, threshold amount of goods or services within that state
questions.explanationJa: 事業体は設立州以外の州でも事業を行うことができ、それだけで課税関係が生じるわけではない。ネクサスとは、事業体と州との間に、その州が事業体に課税できるだけの十分な結びつきがあることをいう。ネクサスが成立すると、事業体はその州の売上税や所得税の義務を負う。ネクサスを生む活動には、倉庫や支店などの物理的拠点の保有、州内で役務を行う従業員の存在、一定額以上の販売がある。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.32

questions.stem:
A C corporation conducted all of its business activities in States A and B and generated $1 million of pretax income in Year 1. The tax rate is 10% in State A and 5% in State B. Both states apportion the taxable income of multistate corporations by employing an equally-weighted three-factor apportionment formula. Neither state allows a tax deduction for state corporate income taxes. At the end of Year 1, the corporation reported the following percentages for its activities in each state for the purpose of calculating the state apportionment factors:

State A | State B
Payroll expense | 50% | 50%
Sales | 75% | 25%
Net property value | 25% | 75%

What is the corporation's Year 1 state apportionment ratio for State B?
questions.explanation:
Corporations operating in multiple states are required to apportion their business income among the states in which they operate. Without apportionment, the same income would be subject to tax in each state.

States generally set their apportionment formula based on three factors: sales, payroll, and property. Several states use an equally weighted three-factor formula. However, some states use a double-weighted sales factor or a single-sales-factor formula. Each factor is calculated as the percentage of that item within the state.

The equally weighted three-factor formula adds each of the three factors and divides by three to arrive at the apportionment factor. The apportionment factor is then multiplied by the total income to determine the amount apportioned to the state.

In this scenario, the percentage for each factor (Statewide property / Total property) is provided. Therefore, the apportionment is found by calculating the average of the percentages for each factor. State B has an apportionment factor of 50% [(0.50 payroll + 0.25 sales + 0.75 property) / 3].

Note:
Corporations operating in multiple states are required to apportion their business income among the states in which they operate. States generally base their formula on three factors: sales, payroll, and property. The equally weighted three-factor formula adds the percentages for each factor and divides by three.
questions.explanationJa: 複数州で事業を行う法人は、同じ所得が各州で重複課税されないよう、事業所得を各州に配分する。均等加重の3要素方式では、売上・給与・資産の各要素の州内割合を合計して3で割り、配分比率を求める。State Bの配分比率は（給与50% + 売上25% + 資産75%）÷ 3 = 50%である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.33

questions.stem: Rigg, Steele, and Urco, all accrual-basis, calendar-year C corporations, have only voting common stock outstanding. Rigg owns 85 percent of Steele and 40 percent of Urco. Steele owns 50 percent of Urco. Which group of corporations qualifies as an affiliated group and may join in the filing of a consolidated federal income tax return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rigg and Urco.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Urco and Steele.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rigg, Steele, and Urco.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An affiliated group does not exist.

questions.explanation:
Generally, an affiliated group of C corporations consists of one or more corporations with a common parent corporation in which all the following conditions are met:

The common parent directly owns at least 80% (by voting power and value of outstanding stock) of one subsidiary within the group.

Each subsidiary is at least 80% directly owned by the group, where corporations within the group (members) can combine direct ownership to meet the 80% minimum.

Because Rigg directly owns 85% of Steele, Rigg and Steele meet the first and second requirements, respectively; therefore, both qualify as an affiliated group. In addition, Urco is 90% directly owned by combining two members (50% by Steele and 40% by Rigg). Urco thus meets the second requirement and qualifies to be included. Therefore, all three corporations qualify as an affiliated group and may elect to file a consolidated return.
questions.explanationJa: 関連グループが成立するには、共通親会社が少なくとも1社の子会社の80%以上を直接所有し、かつ各子会社がグループメンバーにより合計で80%以上直接所有されている必要がある。RiggはSteeleの85%を直接所有するため、両社は要件を満たす。UrcoはRigg（40%）とSteele（50%）の合計で90%を所有されており、グループに含まれる。したがってRigg、Steele、Urcoの3社が関連グループとして連結納税を選択できる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.34

questions.stem: Dahl Corp. was organized and commenced operations in Year 1. At December 31, Year 6, Dahl had $0 taxable income and accumulated earnings and profits of $9,000 before dividend declaration and distribution. On December 31, Year 6, Dahl distributed cash of $9,000 and a vacant parcel of land to Green, Dahl's only stockholder. At the date of distribution, the land had a basis of $5,000 and a fair market value of $40,000. What was Green's taxable dividend income in Year 6 from these distributions?
questions.explanation:
For tax purposes, a C corporation distribution is a dividend up to the distributing corporation's earnings and profits (E&P). Recipient shareholders include the dividend (amount of cash or fair market value [FMV] of property received) in their taxable income. Distributions in excess of E&P are return of capital distributions to the recipient shareholders.

E&P is calculated by first determining the distributing corporation's taxable income. If a corporation makes a nonliquidating distribution of appreciated property, the corporation treats the distribution as a sale and recognizes a gain (property FMV − adjusted basis). This gain increases taxable income and, in turn, E&P.

In this scenario, Dahl Corp.'s $9,000 E&P was increased by $35,000 of taxable gain from distributing appreciated land ($40,000 FMV − $5,000 basis), resulting in $44,000 of pre-distribution E&P. The total amount distributed to Green was $49,000 ($9,000 cash + $40,000 FMV land), and it was taxable dividend income up to Dahl's $44,000 E&P. The remaining $5,000 was a return of capital distribution to Green.
questions.explanationJa: C法人の分配は、法人のE&Pの範囲で配当となり、株主は受け取った現金額または資産の時価を課税所得に含める。法人が値上がり資産を非清算分配すると売却とみなして利得を認識し、その利得が課税所得とE&Pを増やす。Dahl Corp.のE&P$9,000は、土地分配の利得$35,000（$40,000 − $5,000）で増えて分配前$44,000となる。Greenへの分配総額$49,000（現金$9,000 + 土地時価$40,000）のうち$44,000が配当所得となり、残り$5,000は資本の払戻しである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.35

questions.stem: Lite-Mart, a C corporation, had a beginning credit balance in its warranty reserve account of $120,000. During the year, Lite-Mart accrued estimated warranty expense of $16,000. At the end of the year, Lite-Mart's warranty reserve had a $90,000 credit balance. What amount of warranty expense should Lite-Mart deduct?
questions.explanation:
For book purposes, warranty costs are estimated, accrued, and expensed each accounting period (matching principle). However, for taxes, only actual warranty claims incurred and paid during the current period are deductible.

In this scenario, the easiest way to solve for Lite-Mart's deductible warranty expense is to reconstruct the T-account for the warranty reserve account (estimated warranty liability). The cash paid for warranty claims during the year is $46,000

120,000 + 16,000 - 90,000 = 46,000
questions.explanationJa: 帳簿上は製品保証費用を見積もって当期に計上するが、税務上は当期に実際に発生・支払った保証費だけが損金となる。保証引当金の勘定を再構成すると、期首残高$120,000に当期繰入$16,000を加え、期末残高$90,000を差し引いた額が当期の支払額となる。$120,000 + $16,000 − $90,000 = $46,000が、Lite-Martが控除できる保証費用である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.36

questions.stem: A corporation transferred fully depreciated machinery to an individual shareholder in a liquidating distribution. The original cost of the machinery was $6,000, and the fair market value at the date of the transfer was $5,000. If the shareholder's basis in the corporation's stock was $2,000, then the shareholder reports

choices.label: A
choices.text: $3,000 capital gain.

choices.label: B
choices.text: $3,000 ordinary income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: $5,000 ordinary income and $2,000 capital loss.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No gain and no loss.

questions.explanation:
When a corporation distributes property in a complete liquidation, the distribution is treated as a sale or exchange for the shareholder's stock. The sale is valued at the property's FMV (less any liabilities assumed) on the date of distribution.

If the property's FMV (less any liabilities assumed) plus cash received is greater than a shareholder's stock basis, the shareholder recognizes a gain. If the amount is less than stock basis, a loss is recognized. Because stock is a capital asset to the shareholder, any gain or loss recognized is a capital gain or loss (not ordinary income or loss).

In this scenario, a shareholder received property with a FMV of $5,000 as a liquidating distribution. Because the property's FMV is greater than the shareholder's $2,000 stock basis, a $3,000 ($5,000 − $2,000) capital gain is recognized.

("$5,000 ordinary income and $2,000 capital loss.") Ordinary income of $5,000 and a $2,000 capital loss erroneously treat the $5,000 FMV as Section 1245 depreciation recapture and the stock basis as a capital loss. Because the equipment is fully depreciated, the corporation (not the shareholder) would have ordinary income of $5,000 resulting from the deprecation recapture.
questions.explanationJa: 完全清算の分配は、株主にとって株式の売却・交換として扱われ、受け取った資産の時価（引き受けた負債を除く）で評価される。株式は資本資産なので、生じる損益は資本損益であり通常所得ではない。株主は時価$5,000の資産を受け取り、株式簿価$2,000を上回るため、$5,000 − $2,000 = $3,000のキャピタルゲインを認識する。全額償却済みの機械の減価償却リキャプチャー$5,000は法人側の通常所得であり、株主の通常所得ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.37

questions.stem: Parent Company X and subsidiary Company Y file a calendar year consolidated federal income tax return. Company X reported a $120,000 tax loss, which included a $10,000 dividend from Company Y. Company Y reported $140,000 of taxable income before any special deductions, which included $30,000 of dividends received from less than 20% owned stock investments. Neither company took into account any applicable dividends received deduction. What is the group's consolidated tax loss for the year?
questions.explanation:
Because Company X is the affiliate group's parent, it must own at least 80% of Company Y; therefore, Company X may deduct 100% of dividends received from Company Y ($10,000 = $10,000 × 100%). This demonstrates the concept that affiliated corporations eliminate intercompany transactions. Therefore, Company X's portion of income is:

($130,000) | = | ($120,000) unadjusted loss − $10,000 DRD

Company Y owns less than 20% of the corporation from which it received dividends. Accordingly, Company Y can deduct 50% of the dividends received ($15,000 = $30,000 × 50%); therefore, Company Y's portion of income is:

$125,000 | = | $140,000 unadjusted income − $15,000 DRD

Company X and Company Y's consolidated income after DRDs is:

($5,000): = / ($130,000) Company X's loss + $125,000 Company Y's income
questions.explanationJa: 連結納税ではグループ内取引を消去するため、親会社Xが子会社Yから受け取った配当$10,000は全額控除される。Xの損失は$120,000の損失から$10,000を差し引いた$130,000の損失となる。Yは20%未満所有の株式から$30,000の配当を受けているので、50%の受取配当控除$15,000を差し引き、所得は$140,000 − $15,000 = $125,000となる。連結では$130,000の損失と$125,000の所得を合算し、$5,000の損失となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.38

questions.stem: Birch Corp. is an accrual-basis, calendar-year C corporation. Its reported book income before federal income taxes was $250,000, which included $46,000 in municipal bond interest income. Birch's book expenses included $4,000 of interest incurred on indebtedness used to carry the municipal bonds. What should be the amount of Birch's taxable income, as reconciled on Birch's Schedule M-1, Reconciliation of Income (Loss) per Books with Income per Return, of Form 1120, U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return?
questions.explanation:
Although municipal bond interest income is included in book income, it is excluded from taxable income. Expenses deducted on the books related to the production of nontaxable income (interest expense incurred on indebtedness for municipal bonds) are not deductible for tax purposes. These are both permanent differences that will not reverse over time. Therefore, Birch's taxable income is $208,000.

Net income per the books | $250,000
+ Nondeductible interest expense on bonds | 4,000
− Nontaxable municipal bond interest | (46,000)
Taxable income | $208,000
questions.explanationJa: 地方債の利息は帳簿利益に含まれるが課税所得からは除外され、非課税所得を得るための支出（地方債保有のための借入利息）も税務上は損金にならない。いずれも将来解消しない永久差異である。帳簿利益$250,000に損金不算入の支払利息$4,000を加え、非課税の地方債利息$46,000を差し引くと、課税所得は$208,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.39

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly represents the tax effect of the liquidation of an 80% or more owned subsidiary?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The subsidiary can recognize a loss on depreciated assets transferred to minority shareholders.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assets transferred to the parent of the liquidating corporation generally have a carryover basis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The total basis of assets transferred to the parent of the liquidating corporation must be allocated among the various assets according to their fair market values.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The subsidiary recognizes gain on the distribution of appreciated assets to the parent.

questions.explanation:
In a subsidiary liquidation:

The parent and subsidiary do not recognize gain or loss on property distributions to the parent ("The subsidiary recognizes gain on the distribution of appreciated ass…").

The parent's basis in the property equals the subsidiary's basis (carryover basis) ("The total basis of assets transferred to the parent of the liquidatin…").

The parent keeps the subsidiary's tax attributes (NOL, capital loss and charitable contribution carryovers, earnings and profits).

If a subsidiary has minority shareholders (shareholders other than parent), the liquidation is nontaxable only with respect to distributions to the parent. Minority shareholders are treated as if they sold their stock for the distributed assets in a taxable sale. Additionally, the subsidiary recognizes gain but not loss on liquidating distributions made to minority shareholders
questions.explanationJa: 80%以上所有の子会社を清算する場合、親会社への資産分配について親会社も子会社も損益を認識しない。親会社が受け取る資産の簿価は子会社の簿価をそのまま引き継ぐ（引継ぎ簿価）ため、時価で配分し直すことはない。少数株主への分配は課税取引となり、子会社は利得を認識するが損失は認識できない。したがって、親会社に移転した資産が原則として引継ぎ簿価となるという記述が正しい。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.40

questions.stem:
Cannoli Corp. is the parent of its subsidiary, Strudel Corp. Cannoli and Strudel have filed consolidated tax returns since Year 3. In Year 4, Strudel sells land worth $90,000 with a basis of $50,000 to Cannoli at a selling price of $90,000. In Year 6, Cannoli sells the land to an unrelated third party for $120,000. What amount of gain is recognized on Cannoli and Strudel's Year 4 and Year 6 consolidated tax returns, respectively?
Year 4 | Year 6
questions.explanation: In Year 4, Strudel Corp.'s $40,000 gain ($90,000 sale − $50,000 basis) from the intercompany sale to Cannoli Corp. is eliminated (not recognized) on Year 4's consolidated tax return. However, Strudel's $50,000 basis for the land carries over to Cannoli, which will determine any gain/loss when sold. Because the land was sold to an unrelated party in Year 6, Cannoli recognized a $70,000 gain ($120,000 sale − $50,000 carried over basis) on Year 6's consolidated tax return.
questions.explanationJa: 連結納税では、グループ内の資産売却による利得は消去され、その年には認識されない。Year 4にStrudelがCannoliへ売却した土地の利得$40,000（$90,000 − $50,000）は認識されず、Strudelの簿価$50,000がCannoliに引き継がれる。Year 6にCannoliが外部へ$120,000で売却した時点で、$120,000 − $50,000 = $70,000の利得を連結申告で認識する。したがってYear 4は$0、Year 6は$70,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.41

questions.stem: Robin, a C corporation, had revenues of $417,500 and operating expenses of $75,000. Robin also received a $20,000 dividend from a domestic corporation and is entitled to a $10,000 dividend-received deduction. Robin donated $50,000 to a qualified charitable organization in the current year. What is Robin's contribution deduction?
questions.explanationJa: 法人の寄附金控除は、実際の寄附額と調整後課税所得（ATI）の10%のいずれか少ない額に制限され、超過分は5年間繰り越せる。ATIは寄附金控除、NOL・資本損失の繰戻し、受取配当控除を差し引く前の課税所得である。RobinのATIは収入$417,500 + 受取配当$20,000 − 営業費用$75,000 = $362,500で、その10%は$36,250となる。寄附額$50,000より少ないため、控除額は$36,250である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.42

questions.stem: In April, A and B formed X Corp. A contributed $50,000 cash, and B contributed land worth $70,000 (with an adjusted basis of $40,000). B also received $20,000 cash from the corporation. A and B each received 50% of the corporation's stock. What is the tax basis of the land to X Corp?
questions.explanation:
If the transfer is nontaxable, the shareholder's adjusted tax basis (not FMV) for the contributed property carries over to the corporation. However, if the shareholder receives cash or other property (boot)in addition to stock from the corporation, gain up to the boot received is recognized by the shareholder. When this occurs, the carryover basis to the corporation is increased by the shareholder's gain recognized.

In this scenario, A and B transfer cash and property for 100% control (≥ 80%), resulting in a nontaxable exchange. However, because B also received $20,000 cash, B recognizes a $20,000 gain ($20,000 boot received). Therefore, X Corp has $60,000 basis in the land received, which is B's $40,000 carryover basis plus B's $20,000 recognized gain.
questions.explanationJa: 非課税の資産拠出では、法人は拠出者の調整後簿価を引き継ぐが、拠出者が株式以外に現金等（ブート）を受け取ると、ブートの額を限度に拠出者が利得を認識し、法人の引継ぎ簿価もその利得の分だけ増える。AとBは現金と財産を拠出して100%を支配するので交換は非課税だが、Bは現金$20,000を受け取ったため$20,000の利得を認識する。X Corpの土地の簿価は、Bの簿価$40,000に認識利得$20,000を加えた$60,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.43

questions.stem:
Lark owns 10% of Baltic Corp., a calendar year end C corporation. On June 30, Year 2, Baltic made a $250,000 pro rata cash distribution to its stockholders. Baltic had a $40,000 deficit in accumulated earnings and profits on January 1, Year 2, and current earnings and profits for Year 2 are as follows:

1st quarter | $110,000
2nd quarter | (10,000)
3rd quarter | 80,000
4th quarter | 60,000
$240,000:

What portion of Lark's June 30 distribution would be classified as a nontaxable return of capital, assuming that Lark's tax basis in Baltic stock is $20,000?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Baltic Corp. made a distribution of $250,000. The distribution is a $240,000 dividend and $10,000 ROC, as shown below:

CEP | $240,000
Less dividends | (250,000)
Dividends treated as ROC | ($10,000)

For each shareholder, 4% ($10,000 ROC / $250,000 distribution) of the distribution is a nontaxable ROC. Because Lark owns 10% and received a $25,000 ($250,000 × 10%) distribution, Lark would report $1,000 ($25,000 × 4%) as a nontaxable ROC.
questions.explanationJa: Baltic Corp.の当期E&Pは$240,000、累積E&Pは赤字であり、$250,000の分配のうち$240,000が配当、残り$10,000が資本の払戻しとなる。各株主にとって分配の4%（$10,000 ÷ $250,000）が非課税の資本の払戻しにあたる。Larkは10%を所有し$25,000（$250,000 × 10%）を受け取ったので、非課税の資本の払戻しは$25,000 × 4% = $1,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.44

questions.stem:
Clark and Hunt organized Jet Corp. with authorized voting common stock of $400,000. Clark contributed $60,000 cash. Both Clark and Hunt transferred other property in exchange for Jet stock as follows:

Adjusted basis | Fair market value | % of Jet stock
Clark | $ 50,000 | $100,000 | 40%
Hunt | 120,000 | 240,000 | 60%

What was Clark's basis in Jet stock?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, the exchange is nontaxable because Clark and Hunt transferred property and cash, received solely stock, and owned 100% of Jet Corp. after the exchange. Clark's stock basis was $110,000 ($60,000 cash plus $50,000 adjusted basis in the property transferred).
questions.explanationJa: ClarkとHuntは財産と現金を拠出して株式のみを受け取り、拠出直後にJet Corp.の100%を所有するため、交換は非課税となる。非課税の交換では、株式の簿価は拠出した現金と財産の調整後簿価の合計となる。Clarkの株式簿価は現金$60,000と財産の簿価$50,000を合わせた$110,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.45

questions.stem: When a company is domiciled in one state but is subject to income tax in multiple states, business income is generally allocated under the Uniform Division of Income for Tax Purposes Act (UDITPA) on the basis of a combination of which of the following ratios?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Average value of real and personal property, number of employees, and sales.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Average value of real and personal property, compensation to employees, and sales.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fair market value of real and personal property, number of employees, and sales.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fair market value of real and personal property, compensation to employees, and sales.

questions.explanation:
Corporations operating in multiple states are required to apportion their business income among the states where nexus is established in accordance with the Uniform Division of Income for Tax Purposes Act (UDITPA). The concept of apportionment is the division of business income earned by an entity in several states to avoid the same income from being taxed by more than one state.

States use an apportionment formula generally based on three factors: sales, payroll, and property. During a tax period, the sales are calculated as follows:

Sales factor is based on total sales by the entity in a state divided by the entity's total sales made everywhere

Payroll factor is based on total compensation paid (not number of employees) in a state by the entity divided by the total compensation paid everywhere ("Average value of real and personal property, number of employees, and…" / "Fair market value of real and personal property, number of employees,…")

Property factor is based on average value (not FMV) of the entity's real and tangible personal property owned or rented by the entity in a state divided by the average value of all real and tangible personal property owned or rented ("Fair market value of real and personal property, compensation to empl…"). When determining the average value, the original cost is used for property that is owned; for rental property, it is generally based on a factor multiplied by the net rents

The three ratios calculated from the factors are added together and divided by three to determine the percentage of business income apportioned each state.
questions.explanationJa: 複数州で事業を行う法人は、UDITPAに基づき、ネクサスのある州に事業所得を配分する。配分式は売上・給与・資産の3要素からなり、売上要素は州内売上 ÷ 全売上で求める。給与要素は従業員数ではなく州内で支払った報酬額を用い、資産要素は時価ではなく州内の不動産・有形動産の平均価額（所有資産は取得原価）を用いる。したがって、不動産・動産の平均価額、従業員への報酬、売上の組合せが正しい。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.46

questions.stem: Which of the following actions would most likely cause a company to establish nexus with a state for state income tax purposes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Selling tangible personal property within the state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hiring independent contractors to solicit sales in the state.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Purchasing raw materials from a supplier within the state.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Buying an office building in the state to conduct business.

questions.explanation:
In general, a state may impose an income tax on a company that is doing business in that state if the company establishes nexus in the state. However, the Interstate Income Act of 1959 allows an entity formed or physically located in one state (its domicile state) to do business in other states without establishing nexus and being subject to those states' income tax laws.

(Note: The term "nexus" is used in tax law to describe a situation in which a business has a tax presence in a particular state.)

The law applies exclusively to orders for tangible personal property (goods) ("Selling tangible personal property within the state."). In addition, the orders must be either:

Solicited by employees who approve the orders and ship the goods from somewhere other than the state where the goods were sold, or

Solicited by independent contractors, and the goods are shipped from somewhere other than the state where the goods were sold ("Hiring independent contractors to solicit sales in the state.").

One action that will establish nexus with a state for that state's income tax laws is an entity's purchase of property (an office building) in that state.

("Purchasing raw materials from a supplier within the state.") Purchasing items from a business located in another state does not establish nexus with that state.
questions.explanationJa: 州は、州内でネクサスを有する企業に所得税を課すことができる。ただしInterstate Income Act of 1959により、有形動産の注文の勧誘にとどまり、注文の承認と出荷が州外から行われる場合は、従業員による勧誘でも独立請負人による勧誘でもネクサスは生じない。他州の業者から原材料を購入するだけでもネクサスは成立しない。これに対し、州内で事業を行うために事務所ビルを購入すれば、その州でのネクサスが成立する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.47

questions.stem: During the year, Perkins and Fields formed a corporation, with each receiving 50% of the corporate stock. Perkins contributed $100,000 cash, and Fields contributed a building worth $130,000 (with a cost of $110,000 and an adjusted basis of $60,000). Fields also received $30,000 cash from the corporation. What is the tax basis of the building to the corporation?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, Perkins and Fields transfer cash and property for 100% control ( ≥ 80%), resulting in a nontaxable exchange. However, Fields also received $30,000 cash and thus recognizes a $30,000 gain ($130,000 FMV − $60,000 basis = $70,000 gain, limited to $30,000 boot received). Therefore, the corporation has $90,000 basis in the building received, which is Fields's $60,000 carryover basis plus the $30,000 recognized gain.
questions.explanationJa: PerkinsとFieldsは現金と財産を拠出して100%を支配するため、交換は非課税となる。ただしFieldsは現金$30,000を受け取っており、実現利得$70,000（$130,000 − $60,000）のうちブートの$30,000を限度に利得を認識する。法人の建物の簿価は、Fieldsの調整後簿価$60,000に認識利得$30,000を加えた$90,000である。取得原価$110,000は簿価の計算には使わない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.48

questions.stem:
Beta, a C corporation, reported the following items of income and expense for the year:

Gross income: $600,000
Dividend income from a 30% owned domestic corporation: 100,000
Operating expenses: 400,000

What is Beta's taxable income for the year?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, Beta owns 30% of the investee corporation, resulting in a potential DRD of $65,000 ($100,000 dividend income × 65% DRD percentage). Beta's TI before the DRD is $300,000 ($600,000 gross income + $100,000 dividend income − $400,000 operating expenses). Because the potential $65,000 DRD is less than the TI limitation of $195,000 (65% × $300,000), the full amount is deductible. The corporation's TI is $235,000 ($300,000 TI − $65,000 DRD).
questions.explanationJa: Betaは配当支払会社の30%を所有するため、受取配当控除の割合は65%であり、控除額は$100,000 × 65% = $65,000となる。受取配当控除前の課税所得は$600,000 + $100,000 − $400,000 = $300,000である。控除額$65,000は課税所得基準の上限$195,000（$300,000 × 65%）を下回るので全額控除でき、課税所得は$300,000 − $65,000 = $235,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.49
