questions.stem: Pope, a C corporation, owns 15% of Arden Corporation. Arden paid a $3,000 cash dividend to Pope. What is the amount of Pope's dividends received deduction?
questions.explanation:
Pope recognizes dividend income received from Arden and calculates its DRD by multiplying the income by a percentage based on ownership in Arden. Pope owns less than 20%, its DRD is 50% of dividends received.

Here, Pope received a $3,000 dividend from Arden. Pope owns 15% (less than 20%) of Arden; thus, its DRD is $1,500 ($3,000 cash dividend × 50%).
questions.explanationJa: 法人の受取配当控除は、受取配当に配当支払会社の所有割合に応じた率を掛けて求める。所有割合が20%未満の場合、控除率は50%である。PopeはArdenの15%を所有するため、受取配当控除は$3,000 × 50% = $1,500となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.50

questions.stem: Wallace purchased 500 shares of Kingpin, Inc., 15 years ago for $25,000. Wallace has worked as an owner/employee and owned 40% of the company throughout this time. This year, Kingpin, which is not an S corporation, redeemed 100% of Wallace's stock for $200,000. What is the treatment and amount of income or gain that Wallace should report, if any?

choices.label: B
choices.text: $175,000 long-term capital gain.

choices.label: C
choices.text: $175,000 ordinary income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: $200,000 long-term capital gain.

questions.explanation: In this scenario, all of Wallace's stock is redeemed during the current year. This qualifies the redemption to be treated as an exchange, resulting in a capital gain. Accordingly, Wallace recognizes a $175,000 ($200,000 redemption proceeds − $25,000 basis) capital gain. Because the stock was held longer than 1 year, the capital gain is long term.
questions.explanationJa: Wallaceは保有株式の100%を償還されており、この完全償還は交換として扱われるため、配当ではなく譲渡益となる。譲渡益は償還代金$200,000から取得価額$25,000を差し引いた$175,000である。株式の保有期間は1年を超えているので、長期キャピタルゲインとなる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.51

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding the calculation of a C corporation's taxable income and tax liability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Business bad debts are allowed as an ordinary business deduction if the direct write-off method is used.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Charitable contributions are considered a special deduction rather than part of ordinary business deductions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The foreign tax credit is applied to taxable income before multiplying by the tax rate to determine gross tax liability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The dividends received deduction is used to determine income before NOL and special deductions.

questions.explanation: For book purposes, business bad debts (credit losses) are estimated based on the expected collectability of customer accounts (allowance method). However, for tax purposes, only the direct write-off method is permitted.
questions.explanationJa: 帳簿上、事業上の貸倒れは顧客債権の回収可能性に基づいて見積もる（貸倒引当金法）。これに対し税務上は直接償却法しか認められず、実際に貸倒れとなった時点で通常の事業上の控除として損金算入する。したがって、直接償却法を用いる場合に事業上の貸倒れが通常の事業控除として認められるという記述が正しい。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.52

questions.stem: A nonliquidating distribution from a C corporation may be treated by the shareholder as each of the following except

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ordinary income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nontaxable return of capital.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capital gain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Capital loss.

questions.explanation:
Because a nonliquidating distribution does not terminate a shareholder's ownership, the tax treatment depends on the corporation's earnings and profits (E&P) and the shareholder's stock basis.

Generally, distributions are taxable as dividends (ordinary income) to the extent of positive E&P ("Ordinary income."). If the distribution exceeds E&P, the remainder reduces the shareholders' bases in their stock as a nontaxable return of capital (ROC) ("Nontaxable return of capital."). Any excess greater than stock basis is treated as a taxable capital gain since the stock is considered a capital asset ("Capital gain.").

Liquidating distributions terminate the corporation, and the shareholders treat the proceeds as the sale price for their stock. Therefore, shareholders recognize either a capital gain or loss based on the difference between stock basis at the time of the liquidation and the liquidation proceeds.

For a corporate shareholder, dividends will be taxed at ordinary income rates, while an individual shareholder is generally taxed at lower qualified dividend rates.
questions.explanationJa: 非清算分配では株主の所有関係が終わらないため、課税関係は法人のE&Pと株主の株式簿価で決まる。分配はまずプラスのE&Pの範囲で配当（通常所得）となり、E&Pを超える部分は株式簿価を減らす非課税の資本の払戻しとなり、さらに簿価を超える部分はキャピタルゲインとなる。キャピタルロスが生じるのは、株主が清算分配を株式の売却代金として扱い、簿価が受取額を上回る場合である。したがって非清算分配でキャピタルロスとなることはない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.53

questions.stem: Which of the following items should be included as a permanent difference on Schedule M-3, Net Income (Loss) Reconciliation for Corporations With Total Assets of $10 Million or More to reconcile book income to taxable income?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Section 179 election to expense depreciable property.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rent received in advance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Municipal bond interest.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tax credits.

questions.explanation:
A corporation with total assets of $10 million or more reconciles book income to taxable income on Schedule M-3 to account for these differences.

There are two types of differences:

Temporary differences result from the same item's being calculated differently for accounting (GAAP) than for tax purposes (different depreciation or income recognition methods) in any given reporting period ("Section 179 election to expense depreciable property." / "Rent received in advance."). Temporary differences work themselves out over time.

Permanent differences are items that are income or deductions in the year for either book or taxable income but not both (tax-exempt interest). Permanent differences do not reverse over time.

These differences are either added to or subtracted from book income to determine taxable income.
questions.explanationJa: 総資産$10 million以上の法人は、Schedule M-3で帳簿利益と課税所得の差異を調整する。差異のうち一時差異は、減価償却や収益認識の方法が帳簿と税務で異なることで生じ、時間の経過で解消する。Section 179による即時償却や前受賃料は一時差異にあたる。地方債利息は帳簿上は収益だが税務上は非課税であり、解消しない永久差異となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.54

questions.stem: As part of a qualified partial liquidation, a C Corporation redeemed some of its stock from an individual shareholder for $120,000. The shareholder's adjusted basis for the stock redeemed was $50,000. At the time of the redemption, the corporation had accumulated and current earnings and profits of $40,000. What is the treatment and amount of income or gain that the shareholder should report, if any?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $40,000 dividend income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: $70,000 capital gain.

choices.label: C
choices.text: $80,000 capital gain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: $40,000 dividend income and $30,000 capital gain.

questions.explanation: In this scenario, the stock redeemed in a partial liquidation is from a noncorporate shareholder (individual); this qualifies the redemption to be treated as an exchange (capital gain). Accordingly, the shareholder recognizes a $70,000 ($120,000 redemption proceeds − $50,000 basis) capital gain.
questions.explanationJa: 部分清算に伴う償還で、株主が法人ではなく個人であれば、その償還は交換として扱われ、配当ではなく譲渡益となる。E&Pが$40,000あっても配当所得は生じない。株主の譲渡益は償還代金$120,000から株式簿価$50,000を差し引いた$70,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.55

questions.stem: Iron Corporation, a calendar-year S corporation, owns 90% of the voting stock of Silver Corporation. On June 30, Year 3, Gold and Silver, calendar-year domestic C corporations, merged, resulting with Gold as a subsidiary of Silver. Silver owns 80% of Gold's voting stock. Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the companies' ability to file a consolidated return for Year 3?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Silver and Iron may file a consolidated tax return.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Silver and Gold may file a consolidated tax return.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gold and Iron may file a consolidated tax return.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Silver, Gold, and Iron may file a consolidated tax return.

questions.explanation:
An affiliated group exists when:

One C corporation (the parent) owns at least 80 percent of the value of another C corporation's outstanding voting stock, and

All other member C corporations are at least 80% owned by the parent and/or other group members.

S corporations may own stock in a C corporation. Ownership of 80% or more establishes an affiliated group relationship. However, the S corporation parent cannot be included as a member of the affiliated group for federal tax purposes because S corporations are pass-through entities. Therefore, a C corporation and an S corporation may not file a consolidated tax return. A subsidiary C corporation can elect to file a consolidated tax return with its parent, resulting in an affiliated group that is treated as a single taxpayer.

In this scenario, only the Silver and Gold corporations (parent and subsidiary) qualify as an affiliated group and may file a consolidated return. Although Iron owns 90% of Silver Corporation's voting stock, Iron is not a member of the affiliated group because it is an S corporation and therefore ineligible
questions.explanationJa: 関連グループは、親会社となるC法人が他のC法人の議決権株式の80%以上を所有し、他のメンバーも80%以上所有されている場合に成立する。S法人はC法人株式を所有できるが、パススルー事業体なので関連グループのメンバーにはなれず、C法人と連結納税はできない。IronはSilverの90%を所有するがS法人なので除外される。SilverはGoldの80%を所有するため、連結納税ができるのはSilverとGoldである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.56

questions.stem:
As part of a complete liquidation, a C corporation distributed the following assets to unrelated individual shareholders:

Basis | FMV
Investment land | $500,000 | $540,000
Inventory | 130,000 | 150,000
Marketable debt securities | 70,000 | 20,000

What is the amount of capital gain or loss, if any, recognized by the corporation as a result of the liquidation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $10,000 net capital loss.

choices.label: B
choices.text: $10,000 net capital gain.

choices.label: C
choices.text: $40,000 capital gain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No capital gain or loss.

questions.explanation:
In general, when a corporation distributes property to a shareholder in a complete liquidation, the corporation reports gains and losses as if the assets were sold to the shareholder at FMV. The corporation recognizes a gain or loss for the difference between the property's FMV (less any liability assumed by the shareholder) on the date of distribution and property's adjusted basis("No capital gain or loss.").

The type of recognized gain or loss (ie, capital or ordinary) depends on the nature of the asset distributed.

Capital assets (eg, investments in land, marketable debt securities) generate capital gains and losses.

Ordinary income-producing assets (eg, inventory) result in ordinary income or loss.

Section 1231 assets (eg, equipment) are subject to ordinary income depreciation recapture with the remaining balance classified as a capital gain or an ordinary loss.

In this scenario, the corporation distributed only two capital assets (land and securities). Accordingly, the corporation recognizes a $10,000 net capital loss as calculated below:

FMV | Basis | Gain or (loss)
Investment land | $540,000 | $500,000 | $40,000
Marketable debt securities | 20,000 | 70,000 | (50,000)
Net capital loss |  |  | ($10,000)
questions.explanationJa: 完全清算で資産を分配した法人は、時価で売却したものとして、時価と調整後簿価の差額を損益として認識する。損益の性質は資産の種類で決まり、投資用土地や市場性のある債券などの資本資産からは譲渡損益が、棚卸資産からは通常所得が生じる。資本資産は土地と債券の2つであり、土地の利得$40,000（$540,000 − $500,000）と債券の損失$50,000（$20,000 − $70,000）を通算すると$10,000の純資本損失となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.57

questions.stem:
Jans, an individual, owns 80% and 100% of the total value and voting power of A and B Corps., respectively, which in turn own the following (both value and voting power):

Ownership:
Property | A Corp. | B Corp.
Y Corp. | 80% | -
Z Corp. | - | 100%

All companies are C corporations except B Corp., which had elected subchapter S status since inception. Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the companies' ability to file a consolidated return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A, Y, and Z may file as a group.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A and Y may not file as a group, and B and Z may not file as a group.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A and Y may file as a group, and B and Z may file as a group.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A and Y may file as a group, but B and Z may not file as a group.

questions.explanation:
In this scenario, corporations A, Y, and Z are domestic C corporations. B Corp. is a subchapter S corporation and therefore ineligible for affiliation because only C corporations are eligible group members ("A and Y may file as a group, and B and Z may file as a group."). Because Z is wholly owned by B (an ineligible S corporation), it too is ineligible for affiliation ("A, Y, and Z may file as a group.").

A Corp. (a C corporation) owns 80% of Y (another C corporation). Therefore, A and Y are an affiliated group that may elect to file a consolidated tax return
questions.explanationJa: 連結納税の関連グループに加われるのは国内C法人だけである。B Corp.はS法人なので関連グループのメンバーになれず、Bに100%所有されるZもグループを組む親会社がいないため連結できない。A Corp.はC法人であるYの80%を所有するので、AとYは関連グループとして連結納税を選択できる。したがって、AとYはグループとして申告できるが、BとZはできない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.58

questions.stem: In which of the following situations will a controlled foreign corporation located in Ireland be deemed to have Subpart F income?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Services are provided by an Irish company in England under a contract entered into by its U.S. parent.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Property is produced in Ireland by the Irish company and sold outside its country of incorporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Services are performed in Ireland by the Irish company under a contract entered into by its U.S. parent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Property is bought from the controlled foreign corporation's U.S. parent and is sold by an Irish company for use in an Irish manufacturing plant.

questions.explanation:
U.S. entities may conduct foreign business activities through a controlled foreign corporation (CFC). In general, foreign-sourced income is taxable to U.S. taxpayers when repatriation occurs (foreign profits received as dividends). To prevent U.S. parent corporations from using CFCs to defer certain income from U.S. taxation, Subpart F tax provisions were enacted. U.S. taxpayers owning 10% or more of a CFC must include their share of Subpart F income annually in gross income, regardless of whether the share was received.

Subpart F income includes certain foreign-based sales, services, and personal holding company income (PHCI) of a CFC.

For sales, any income received by a CFC from the purchase or sale of personal property involving a related party (U.S. parent corporation) constitutes Subpart F income when the property is manufactured, purchased, sold, or consumed outside the CFC's home country (country of incorporation)

Services are considered Subpart F income when the CFC performs the services (eg, engineering) outside the CFC's home country for/on behalf of the U.S. parent corporation. For example, Subpart F income exists when an Irish CFC provides services to an entity in England under a contract entered into by the CFC's S. parent

Foreign PHCI includes a CFC's income from dividends, interest, annuities, rents, and royalties

("Property is produced in Ireland by the Irish company and sold outside…") The property is produced in Ireland by the Irish CFC; therefore, any profits are not Subpart F income.

("Services are performed in Ireland by the Irish company under a contra…") Because the services are performed in Ireland by the Irish CFC, the income is not Subpart F income.

("Property is bought from the controlled foreign corporation's U.S. par…") Because property bought from the U.S. parent is used by the Irish CFC in Ireland, it is not Subpart F income.
questions.explanationJa: 米国法人が支配外国法人（CFC）を使って所得の米国課税を繰り延べることを防ぐため、Subpart F規定があり、CFCの10%以上を所有する米国株主はSubpart F所得の持分を毎年総所得に含める。役務提供については、CFCが米国親会社のために本国（設立国）外で役務を行うと、Subpart F所得となる。アイルランドのCFCが米国親会社の結んだ契約に基づきイングランドで役務を提供する場合がこれにあたる。アイルランド国内で製造した資産の販売、アイルランド国内での役務、米国親会社から購入しアイルランドの工場で使う資産はいずれも本国内の活動であり、Subpart F所得にならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.59

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes global intangible low-taxed income (GILTI)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: GILTI replaces foreign-derived intangible income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: GILTI is a category of foreign income designed to be taxed immediately.

choices.label: C
choices.text: GILTI replaces the Subpart F income provision for controlled foreign corporations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: GILTI is any income from property sold, leased, or exchanged to any foreign person for a foreign use.

questions.explanation:
Global intangible low-taxed income (GILTI), a new category of foreign-earned income for U.S.-controlled foreign corporations (CFCs). GILTI is designed to prevent erosion of the U.S. tax base by discouraging multinational companies from shifting their profits on intangible assets to foreign jurisdictions with lower tax rates.

A shareholder's GILTI is taxed at a low rate immediately rather than being deferred and taxed at a higher rate. Although GILTI is intended to approximate the income from intangible assets (patents, trademarks, or copyrights) that are held abroad, it is assessed using a complex calculation that determines a minimum tax on the profits of CFCs.

("GILTI replaces foreign-derived intangible income.") GILTI does not replace foreign-derived intangible income, which is generated from intangible assets held in the U.S. and derived from serving foreign markets (eg, licensing fees received for U.S.-owned logos printed on T-shirts produced in foreign countries).

("GILTI replaces the Subpart F income provision for controlled foreign…") GILTI does not replace the existing Subpart F income. However, the rules for both income categories are designed to prevent U.S. shareholders of CFCs from deferring income tax on certain foreign income.

("GILTI is any income from property sold, leased, or exchanged to any f…") Foreign-derived deduction eligible income, not GILTI, refers to any deduction eligible income from (1) property sold, leased, licensed, or exchange) to any foreign person for a foreign use, or (2) services provided to any foreign person or with respect to any foreign property.
questions.explanationJa: GILTI（グローバル無形資産低課税所得）は、米国が支配する外国法人（CFC）の所得の新しい区分であり、無形資産の利益を低税率国に移して米国の課税ベースを侵食することを防ぐためのものである。株主のGILTIは繰り延べられず、低い税率で即時に課税される。GILTIは国内保有の無形資産から生じる外国由来無形資産所得（FDII）に代わるものではなく、Subpart F所得の規定に代わるものでもない。外国の者への外国使用目的の資産の販売等から生じる所得は、外国由来控除適格所得の説明である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.60

questions.stem:
Quigley, Roberk, and Storm form a corporation. Quigley exchanges $25,000 of legal services for 30 shares of stock. Roberk exchanges land with a basis of $10,000 and a fair market value of $100,000 for 60 shares of stock. Storm exchanges $10,000 cash for 10 shares of stock. What amount of income should each shareholder recognize?
Quigley | Roberk | Storm
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, Quigley's 30 shares do not count toward control since legal services are not property, so Quigley should recognize $25,000 of income. Roberk and Storm together own 70 of the 100 total shares (70%), which is less than 80%. Therefore, neither controls the corporation, and their exchanges are taxable. Roberk should recognize $90,000 of gain ($100,000 FMV − $10,000 land basis). Because Storm's shares were purchased with cash, no gain or loss is recognized from the taxable transfer of $10,000.

Things to remember:
Property may be transferred to a corporation solely in exchange for stock. A transferor that is in control (owns at least 80%) of the corporation immediately after the exchange will recognize no gain or loss. Services are not property, so shares issued to service providers are not included in determining control.
questions.explanationJa: 役務は財産ではないため、Quigleyが法務サービスの対価として受け取った30株は支配基準の判定に含めず、Quigleyは$25,000の所得を認識する。RoberkとStormの所有は100株中70株（70%）で80%に満たないため、両者の交換は課税取引となる。Roberkは土地の時価$100,000と簿価$10,000の差額$90,000の利得を認識する。Stormは現金で株式を購入したので、課税取引でも損益は生じず$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.61

questions.stem: During the year, a corporation declares a dividend and subsequently distributes to a stockholder $15,000 in cash and a bond with a basis of $25,000 and a fair market value of $26,000 on the date of distribution. The bond had a fair market value of $26,500 on the date that the corporation declared the dividend. The corporation has current earnings and profits in excess of the total amounts distributed during the year. Which of the following identifies the tax consequences of the distribution to the stockholder?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $15,000 of dividend income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: $40,000 of dividend income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: $41,000 of dividend income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: $41,500 of dividend income.

questions.explanation: In this scenario, because the corporation has sufficient E&P, the distribution is taxable as dividend income to the shareholder. The amount of income equals the $15,000 cash and $26,000 FMV of the bonds on the date of the distribution (not the date the dividend was declared) ("$41,500 of dividend income."). Therefore, the shareholder reports dividend income of $41,000 ($15,000 + $26,000).
questions.explanationJa: 法人のE&Pは分配総額を上回っているため、分配は株主の配当所得として課税される。資産の分配による配当額は、配当宣言日ではなく分配日の時価で測定する。株主の配当所得は現金$15,000と分配日の債券時価$26,000の合計$41,000である。宣言日の時価$26,500は使わない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.62

questions.stem:
A corporation has book net income before federal income taxes of $630,000 for the current year. The following items are included in net income:

Life insurance premiums paid for policies on key employees (corporation is the owner and beneficiary): $10,000
Accrued warranty expense: 15,000
Environmental fines: 25,000

The total amount of warranty claims during the year is $8,500. What is the taxable income the corporation will report on Schedule M-1?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, all three items (life insurance premium payments, accrued warranty expense, fines) are nondeductible for taxes. These amounts are added back to the corporation's NI on Schedule M-1. However, a deduction is allowed for the $8,500 in warranty claims paid during the year. Therefore, the corporation will report TI on Schedule M-1 of $671,500, as shown below:

Net income | $630,000
Add back nondeductible expenses:
Life insurance premiums paid | 10,000
Accrued warranty expense | 15,000
Environmental fines | 25,000
Deduct warranty claims paid | (8,500)
Taxable income | $671,500
questions.explanationJa: 役員保険の保険料、未払計上した製品保証費用、環境罰金の3項目はいずれも税務上損金とならないため、Schedule M-1で帳簿利益に加算する。一方、当期に実際に支払った保証費$8,500は損金算入できる。課税所得は$630,000 + $10,000 + $15,000 + $25,000 − $8,500 = $671,500である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.64

questions.stem: Each of the following statements regarding the tax implications for a foreign subsidiary or a foreign branch is correct, except:

choices.label: A
choices.text: A foreign branch's net income is subject to U.S federal income tax.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A U.S. corporation receiving dividends from a foreign subsidiary is generally eligible for a 100% dividends received deduction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A foreign subsidiary's net income is not subject to U.S. federal income tax.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A U.S. parent company of a foreign subsidiary may use the losses of the subsidiary to offset its income.

questions.explanation:
Foreign subsidiaries and foreign branches have different tax consequences. Since a foreign branch is merely an extension of a U.S. corporation that conducts business outside of the U.S, its net income is included in the tax return of the U.S. corporation. Accordingly, branches are subject to U.S. federal income tax and may generate foreign tax credits ("A foreign branch's net income is subject to U.S federal income tax.").

A foreign subsidiary is a separate legal entity incorporated under the laws of the foreign country where it is located. Although the foreign subsidiary may be partially or wholly owned by a U.S corporation, it cannot file a consolidated U.S tax return with its U.S. parent company. Therefore, a U.S. parent of a foreign subsidiary may not use the losses of the subsidiary to offset its income.

A foreign subsidiary's net income is subject to the foreign country's tax system, not U.S. taxation ("A foreign subsidiary's net income is not subject to U.S. federal inco…"). However, to encourage the repatriation of foreign income, the U.S. tax codes allows for a 100% dividends received deduction (referred to as the participation exemption) for foreign-sourced dividends paid to U.S. corporations
questions.explanationJa: 外国支店は米国法人の延長にすぎないため、その純利益は米国法人の申告に含まれて米国連邦所得税の対象となり、外国税額控除も生じうる。外国子会社は外国法に基づいて設立された別個の法人であり、その純利益は現地国で課税され、米国の連邦所得税の対象とはならない。米国親会社と連結申告することもできないため、親会社は子会社の損失を自社の所得と相殺できない。なお外国子会社からの配当については、米国法人に原則100%の受取配当控除が認められる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.65

questions.stem: If an S corporation has no accumulated earnings and profits, the amount distributed to a shareholder

choices.label: A
choices.text: Must be returned to the S corporation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increases the shareholder's basis for the stock.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreases the shareholder's basis for the stock.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Has no effect on the shareholder's basis for the stock.

questions.explanation: Distributions to an S corporation shareholder are treated in the same manner as distributions to a partner from a partnership, in that they decrease the investor's basis in the entity.
questions.explanationJa: S法人の株主への分配は、パートナーシップからパートナーへの分配と同様に扱われる。累積E&Pがない場合、分配は株主の株式簿価を減らす。したがって、分配は株主の株式簿価を減少させるという記述が正しい。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.66

questions.stem: Beck Corp. has been a calendar-year S corporation since its inception on January 2, Year 5. On January 1, Year 8, Green and Blue each owned 50% of the Beck stock, in which their respective tax bases were $12,000 and $9,000. For the year ended December 31, Year 8, Beck had $81,000 in ordinary business income and $10,000 in tax-exempt income. Beck made a $51,000 cash distribution to each shareholder on December 31, Year 8. What was Green's tax basis in Beck after the distribution?
questions.explanation:
Each shareholder in an S corporation (a flow-through entity) has a tax basis that is used to determine the deductibility of S corporation losses, the treatment of distributions, and gain or loss on disposition. Basis is adjusted in each accounting period for the shareholder's portion of the corporation's ordinary income/loss, separately stated items (tax-exempt income, nondeductible expenses), additional contributions, and distributions. The shareholder's basis may never fall below zero.

Tax-exempt income increases basis, so the income remains tax-exempt. If basis is not increased, the tax-exempt income will be taxed on the eventual sale of the stock through a larger gain or smaller loss.

In this scenario, Green's basis is $6,500, calculated as follows:

Beginning basis: $ 12,000
Green's share of business income ($81,000 × 50%): 40,500
Green's share of tax-exempt income ($10,000 × 50%): 5,000
Less: Distribution: (51,000)
Ending basis: $ 6,500
questions.explanationJa: S法人の株主の簿価は、通常所得・損失、非課税所得などの区分表示項目、追加出資、分配によって毎期調整され、ゼロを下回ることはない。非課税所得も簿価を増やすことで、将来の株式売却時に課税されないようにしている。Greenの簿価は期首$12,000に事業所得の持分$40,500（$81,000 × 50%）と非課税所得の持分$5,000（$10,000 × 50%）を加え、分配$51,000を差し引いて$6,500となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.67

questions.stem: Dart Corp., a calendar-year S corporation, had 60,000 shares of voting common stock and 40,000 shares of nonvoting common stock issued and outstanding. On February 23, Year 7, Dart filed a revocation statement with the consent of shareholders holding 30,000 shares of its voting common stock. Dart's S corporation election

choices.label: A
choices.text: Did not terminate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Terminated as of January 1, 20X7.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Terminated on February 24, 20X7.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Terminated as of January 1, 20X8.

questions.explanation:
Termination of a corporation's S status can be voluntary or involuntary (termination for no longer meeting the S requirements). A voluntary election requires shareholders holding more than half (>50%) of all shares (including nonvoting shares) on the election date to agree to revocation.

In general, if the election is made within the first 2 1/2 months of the tax year, it is effective the first day of the current year ("Terminated on February 24, 20X7." / "Terminated as of January 1, 20X8."). Otherwise, the revocation is effective on the first day of the following tax year. As an alternative, a specific date on or after the election may be selected.

In this scenario, Dart Corp. has 100,000 shares outstanding (60,000 voting and 40,000 nonvoting). A revocation election requires 50,001 shares to be effective; therefore, consent of 30,000 shares is insufficient to revoke the election ("Terminated as of January 1, 20X7.").
questions.explanationJa: S法人の選択を任意に取り消すには、議決権のない株式も含めた発行済株式の過半数（50%超）を保有する株主の同意が必要である。Dart Corp.の発行済株式は議決権株式60,000株と無議決権株式40,000株の計100,000株であり、取消しには50,001株以上の同意がいる。30,000株の同意では足りないため、S法人の選択は終了していない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.68

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about qualifying shareholders of an S corporation is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A general partnership may be a shareholder.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only individuals may be shareholders.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Individuals, estates, and certain trusts may be shareholders.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nonresident aliens may be shareholders.

questions.explanation:
A corporation may elect to be treated as an S corporation (a flow-through entity) if it meets certain S corporation election requirements:

All shareholders must be individuals, estates, or certain trusts.

The individuals must be either citizens or residents of the U.S. ("Nonresident aliens may be shareholders.").

C corporations, S corporations, partnerships, limited liability companies, and big trusts are not permitted to be shareholders ("A general partnership may be a shareholder.").
questions.explanationJa: S法人を選択するには、株主がすべて個人、遺産財団、または一定の信託でなければならず、個人は米国市民または米国居住者である必要がある。C法人、S法人、パートナーシップ、LLCは株主になれない。したがって、個人・遺産財団・一定の信託が株主になれるという記述が正しく、ジェネラル・パートナーシップや非居住外国人は株主になれない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.69

questions.stem: Absent an election to close the books, the allocation of nonseparately stated income or loss for an S corporation shareholder that changed his ownership interest during the year is computed based on which of the following ownership percentages?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ownership percentage at the end of the S corporation year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ownership percentage computed on a per-share per-day basis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ownership percentage at the beginning of the S corporation year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ownership percentage determined as an average of the beginning and ending ownership percentages.

questions.explanation: The allocation of non-separately stated income or loss for an S corporation shareholder that changed his or her ownership interest during the year is computed based on ownership percentage computed on a per-share per-day basis.
questions.explanationJa: 年の途中で持分が変動したS法人株主への区分表示されない所得・損失の配分は、帳簿締切りの選択がない限り、1株・1日あたりの方法（per-share per-day）で計算した持分割合に基づく。期首や期末の持分割合、あるいは期首と期末の平均を用いるのではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.70

questions.stem: A taxpayer owned 40% of the outstanding stock of a C corporation. During the tax year, the corporation reported $400,000 in taxable income and distributed a total of $70,000 in cash dividends to its shareholders. The taxpayer accurately reported $28,000 in gross income on their individual tax return. If the corporation had been an S corporation and the distributions to the owners had been proportionate, how much income would the taxpayer have reported on their individual return?
questions.explanation:
As a flow-through entity, the S corporation does not pay tax. Instead, the income and separately stated items reported by the S corporation are allocated to the shareholders on Schedules K-1. The shareholders then include their share of the income on their personal tax returns and pay tax on the income, even if it is not distributed.

In this scenario, if the corporation had been an S corporation, the taxpayer would have needed to report their share of the income, $160,000 ($400,000 S corporation income × 40% ownership). The $28,000 distribution is a nontaxable return of capital and will reduce the taxpayer's basis
questions.explanationJa: S法人はパススルー事業体なので法人税を納めず、所得はSchedule K-1で株主に配分され、分配の有無にかかわらず株主の申告で課税される。この法人がS法人であれば、納税者は所得$400,000の40%である$160,000を報告することになる。比例的に受け取った分配$28,000は非課税の資本の払戻しとして株式簿価を減らすだけであり、所得には含めない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.71

questions.stem: Dove and Eagle formed a business entity in which they are equal owners. Dove contributed cash of $100,000, and Eagle contributed land with a basis of $40,000 and fair market value of $100,000. For its first year of operations, the entity had taxable income of $60,000 and made no distributions. At year end it had outstanding recourse liabilities to third parties of $10,000. Eagle had a basis of $70,000 in the entity at the end of the first year of operations. What type of entity was formed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: C corporation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: S corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: General partnership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Limited liability company (LLC).

questions.explanation:
The calculation for basis varies depending on the entity type. In this scenario, basis is determined as follows.

C or S corporations: If the shareholders have control, the shareholder's basis in the stock will be the basis in the property. As a taxable entity, the basis in stock of a C corporation generally stays the same each year. As a flow-through entity, the basis in an S corporation is increased each year by the pro rata share of income.

Partnerships: Initial basis in a partnership is the same as the basis of the property contributed (carryover basis). Basis is increased by the partner's pro rata share of income and recourse debt.

Should an S corporation default on debt, shareholders are not responsible for repaying the entity's debt (limited liability). Therefore, the entity's debt does not increase basis. If a partnership defaults on recourse debt, the lender can seek satisfaction from the partners. Therefore, recourse debt increases basis in a partnership.

In this scenario, Eagle's basis of $70,000 indicates that an S corporation was formed, as noted below.

S corporation | C corporation | Partnership
Control test met | Yes | Yes | N/A
Contribution | $40,000 | $40,000 | $40,000
Income ($60,000 × 50%) | 30,000 | 0 | 30,000
Recourse debt ($10,000 × 50%) | 0 | 0 | 5,000
Ending basis | $70,000 | $40,000 | $75,000
questions.explanationJa: 株主の簿価の計算は事業体の種類で異なる。C法人もS法人も支配基準を満たせば株式簿価は拠出資産の簿価となるが、S法人は毎年所得の持分だけ簿価が増え、C法人は増えない。パートナーシップでは所得の持分に加えてリコース債務の持分も簿価に加わるが、S法人株主は事業体の債務に責任を負わないので債務は簿価に入らない。Eagleの簿価は、S法人なら$40,000 + 所得持分$30,000 = $70,000、C法人なら$40,000、パートナーシップならさらにリコース債務持分$5,000を加えて$75,000となるので、期末簿価$70,000からS法人と判断できる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.72

questions.stem: Which of the following can be an advantage of a limited liability company over an S corporation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Double taxation of profits is avoided.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Owners receive limited liability protection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Appreciated property can be distributed tax-free to an owner.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Incentive stock options can be used to compensate owners.

questions.explanation:
Choice "Appreciated property can be distributed tax-free to an owner." (Correct): An LLC, unlike an S corporation, can generally distribute appreciated property tax-free to an owner.

Choice "Double taxation of profits is avoided." (Incorrect): Both LLCs and S corporations are pass-through entities for federal income tax purposes; therefore, avoiding double taxation of profits is not an advantage of an LLC over an S corporation, as both forms of business organization enjoy this advantage.

Choice "Owners receive limited liability protection." (Incorrect): Both LLCs and S corporations provide limited liability protection for their owners; therefore, limited liability protection is not an advantage of an LLC over an S corporation, as both forms of business organization enjoy this advantage.

Choice "Incentive stock options can be used to compensate owners." (Incorrect): Both LLCs and S corporations can use incentive stock options to compensate owners; therefore, incentive stock options do not constitute an advantage of an LLC over an S corporation.
questions.explanationJa: LLCはS法人と異なり、原則として値上がり資産を課税なしで所有者に分配できる。これがS法人に対するLLCの利点である。二重課税の回避はどちらもパススルー事業体なので共通の特徴であり、有限責任もどちらにも認められる。インセンティブ・ストック・オプションによる報酬もどちらでも使えるため、LLC固有の利点にはならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.73

questions.stem: An S corporation has two shareholders who are also employees of the corporation. Shareholder A owns 20 shares and shareholder B owns 90 shares. The total number of shares issued and outstanding is 2,000. The corporation pays the health insurance premiums for all its employees and families. The cost of family coverage is $5,300. The corporation pays for family coverage for both shareholders. Because the company paid for health insurance, which of the following amounts would be reported to Shareholder A as his income?
questions.explanation:
At 20 shares out of 2,000 total shares, Shareholder A is a 1% shareholder. Because only fringe benefits paid on behalf of a greater-than-2% shareholder are includible in a shareholder-employee's gross income, Shareholder A does not need to report any amount of the family health insurance coverage in income.

Note: Only fringe benefits paid on behalf of a greater-than-2% shareholder are includible in a shareholder-employee's gross income.
questions.explanationJa: Shareholder Aの持株は2,000株中20株で、持分は1%である。S法人が支払うフリンジベネフィットが株主兼従業員の総所得に含まれるのは、2%超の株主の場合だけである。Aは2%超の株主ではないため、家族の医療保険料について所得として報告すべき額は$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.74

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer owned 100% of Alpha Corp., an S corporation. At the beginning of the year, the taxpayer's basis in Alpha was $25,000. Alpha realized ordinary income during the year in the amount of $1,000 and a long-term capital loss in the amount of $3,000 for this year. Alpha distributed $30,000 in cash to the taxpayer during the year. What amount of the $30,000 cash distribution is taxable to the taxpayer?
questions.explanation:
Basis is adjusted during each accounting period--but never below zero--for the shareholder's pro rata share of the calculated ordinary income or loss, separately stated items, contributions, and distributions. Distributions in excess of basis are taxable.

To ensure the proper tax treatment of distributions, basis must be adjusted in the following order:

Increased for income items, including gains

Decreased for distributions

Decreased for nondeductible, noncapital expenses (eg, nondeductible fines) and depletion

Decreased for items of loss and deduction

In this scenario, to determine how much of the $30,000 cash distribution is taxable, the beginning basis of $25,000 is first increased by ordinary income of $1,000, for basis of $26,000. Next, basis is decreased (but not below zero) by the distribution of $30,000. Basis is reduced to zero, and the excess distribution of $4,000 ($30,000 distribution − $26,000 basis) is taxable.

Beginning basis | $25,000
+ Ordinary income | 1,000
Adjusted basis | 26,000
− Distribution* | (30,000)
Ending basis (not below $0) | $0
*Excess distribution of $4,000 ($30,000 distribution − $26,000 basis) is taxable.:

Because basis is already zero, the $3,000 capital loss is suspended until there is sufficient basis to absorb it.
questions.explanationJa: S法人株主の簿価は、所得項目による増加、分配による減少、損金不算入費用による減少、損失・控除項目による減少の順に調整し、ゼロを下回らない。簿価を超える分配は課税される。期首簿価$25,000に通常所得$1,000を加えて$26,000とし、分配$30,000で簿価はゼロとなり、超過分$4,000（$30,000 − $26,000）が課税される。長期キャピタルロス$3,000は簿価がゼロのため繰り越され、簿価が回復するまで使えない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.75

questions.stem: Graphite Corp. has been a calendar-year S corporation since its inception on January 2, Year 1. On January 1, Year 4, Smith and Tyler each owned 50% of Graphite stock in which their respective bases were $12,000 and $9,000. For the year ended December 31, Year 4, Graphite had $80,000 in ordinary business income and $6,000 in tax-exempt income. Graphite made a $53,000 cash distribution to each shareholder on December 31, Year 4. What total amount of income from Graphite is includible in Smith's Year 4 adjusted gross income?
questions.explanation:
S corporations were created to help small, family-owned businesses. In addition to the liability protection of a C corporation, S corporations provide a partnership's single level of taxation.. A corporation may elect to be treated as an S corporation (a flow-through entity) if certain requirements are met.

S corporations do not pay tax as flow-through entities. Instead, the income and separately stated items reported by the S corporation are allocated pro rata to the shareholders on Schedules K-1. The shareholders then include their shares of the income on their personal tax returns and pay tax on the income.

Distributions are generally a non-taxable return of capital if the shareholder has sufficient basis. Tax-exempt interest, a separately stated item, is not included in the shareholder's gross income, but it does increase basis.

In this scenario, Smith owns 50% of Graphite and must include $40,000 (50% × $80,000 ordinary business income) in AGI. Smith's share ($3,000 = $6,000 × 50%) of tax-exempt income is not included in AGI but will increase Smith's basis in Graphite. Because Smith has sufficient basis, the distribution is a nontaxable return of capital and will reduce Smith's basis
questions.explanationJa: S法人はパススルー事業体として法人税を納めず、所得と区分表示項目は持分に応じてSchedule K-1で株主に配分される。非課税所得は株主の総所得に含まれないが、株式簿価は増やす。株主に十分な簿価があれば、分配は非課税の資本の払戻しとなる。SmithのAGIに含まれるのは通常事業所得の持分$40,000（$80,000 × 50%）だけであり、非課税所得の持分$3,000は含まれず、分配も課税されない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.76

questions.stem: Which of the following would cause the termination of S status for an S corporation that is already formed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A partnership becomes a shareholder of the S corporation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The S corporation becomes a partner in a partnership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The S corporation becomes a shareholder in a C corporation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A resident alien becomes a shareholder of the S corporation.

questions.explanation:
Requirements for S corporation election

(Simple and Small and Shareholder pay taxes)

No more than 100 shareholders

Shareholders must be individuals (or certain estates or trusts)

Shareholders must be either S. residents or citizens

Must be a domestic corporation

Only one class of stock is allowed

Termination of a corporation's S status can be voluntary (ie, revocation) or involuntary (no longer meets S status requirements). Termination occurs when the S corporation violates any of the requirements for S status (partnership becomes a shareholder). The termination is effective the day after the disqualifying event.
questions.explanationJa: S法人であるには、株主100人以下、株主は個人（または一定の遺産財団・信託）、株主は米国居住者または市民、国内法人、株式は1種類のみといった要件を満たす必要がある。S法人の地位は、任意の取消しのほか、要件を満たさなくなったときにも終了する。パートナーシップが株主になると株主要件に反するため、S法人の地位は終了する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.77

questions.stem: Which of the following items must be separately stated on Form 1120S, U.S. Income Tax Return for a Corporation, Schedule K-1?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mark-to-market income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Unearned revenue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Section 1245 gain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gain or loss from the sale of collectibles.

questions.explanation:
Separately stated items are not part of ordinary business income/loss because they receive special tax treatment. For example, certain items (capital gains) are taxed at preferential tax rates.

Gains and losses on collectibles are part of the capital gains and losses netting process. Therefore, they would be separately stated items on Schedule K-1.

("Mark-to-market income.") Mark-to-market income does not receive preferential tax treatment for shareholders. Therefore, it is included in nonseparately stated ordinary business net income.

("Unearned revenue.") Unearned revenue is a liability and is reported on the balance sheet, not on Schedule K-1.

("Section 1245 gain.") Gain from the sale of Section 1245 property is treated as ordinary income. Therefore, it does not receive differential tax treatment and is included in the determination of ordinary business net income.

Note: In general, deprecation claimed on section 1245 property is recaptured as ordinary income (not capital gain!) to the extent of gain realized on the property
questions.explanationJa: 区分表示項目は、キャピタルゲインの優遇税率のように株主段階で特別な扱いを受けるため、通常事業所得と分けて記載する。収集品の売却損益はキャピタルゲイン・ロスの通算の対象になるので、Schedule K-1で区分表示しなければならない。時価評価所得は優遇を受けないので通常事業所得に含まれ、前受収益は貸借対照表上の負債でありK-1には載らない。Section 1245の利得は減価償却のリキャプチャーとして通常所得になるため、通常事業所得に含まれる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.78

questions.stem: Pankee Inc, was originally formed as a C corporation and made an S election 5 years ago. Which of the following statements correctly describes taxability of Pankee's distributions to its shareholders?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A distribution to the shareholders will be taxable to the shareholders, if it is treated as coming from the S corporation’s accumulated adjusted account and represents an amount already taxed to the shareholders.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A distribution to the shareholders will be nontaxable to the shareholders, if it is treated as coming from the S corporation’s accumulated adjusted account and represents an amount already taxed to the shareholders.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A distribution to the shareholders will be nontaxable to the shareholders, if it is treated as coming from the S corporation’s accumulated earnings and profits, earned during its years as a C corporation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A distribution to the shareholders will be nontaxable to the shareholders regardless of whether it is treated as coming from the S corporation’s accumulated adjusted account or its accumulated earnings and profits.

questions.explanation: Distributions to shareholders of an S corporation are assumed to first come from the accumulated adjustment account, which is made up of the entity's earnings that have already passed through to shareholders but have not yet been distributed. These distributions are not taxable since they represent amounts that have already been taxed. Excess distributions come from accumulated earnings and profits, which represents earnings of the entity when it had previously been a C corporation that had neither been distributed nor passed through to the shareholders. These distributions are taxable as ordinary dividends. Any additional distributions are considered nontaxable returns of capital until the shareholder's basis has been eliminated, then the remainder treated as a capital gain.
questions.explanationJa: S法人の株主への分配は、まず累積調整勘定（AAA）から行われたものとみなされる。AAAはすでに株主に配分され課税済みだが未分配の利益なので、そこからの分配は非課税である。AAAを超える分配はC法人時代の累積E&Pから行われ、通常の配当として課税される。さらに超える分配は、簿価がなくなるまで非課税の資本の払戻しとなり、残りはキャピタルゲインとなる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.79

questions.stem: Bristol Corp. was formed as a C corporation on January 1, Year 3, and elected S corporation status on January 1, Year 12. At the time of the election, Bristol had accumulated C corporation earnings and profits, which have not been distributed. Bristol has had the same 25 shareholders throughout its existence. In Year 15, Bristol's S election will terminate if it:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increases the number of shareholders to 100.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adds a decedent's estate as a shareholder to the existing shareholders.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Takes a charitable contribution deduction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Has passive investment income exceeding 90% of gross receipts in each of the 3 consecutive years ending December 31, Year 14.

questions.explanation:
Termination for excess passive income occurs when both of these conditions exist:

Passive investment income exceeds 25% of the S corporation's gross receipts for each of 3 consecutive years.

Accumulated earnings and profits are attributable to prior C corporation status.

The termination is effective on the 1st day of the following year.

In this scenario, Bristol Corp. had passive investment income exceeding 90% (>25%) of gross receipts for the 3 years ending December 31, Year 14. The S election will terminate on January 1, Year 15.

("Increases the number of shareholders to 100.") S corporations are permitted to have up to 100 unrelated shareholders.

("Adds a decedent's estate as a shareholder to the existing shareholder…") Certain estates and trusts, including a decedent's estate, are permissible S corporation shareholders.

("Takes a charitable contribution deduction.") S corporations are permitted to make charitable contributions, which pass through to the shareholders to deduct on their tax returns.
questions.explanationJa: 受動的投資所得が多すぎることによるS法人の終了は、C法人時代から引き継いだ累積E&Pがあり、かつ受動的投資所得が3年連続で総収入の25%を超える場合に生じ、翌年の初日に効力を生じる。BristolはC法人時代の累積E&Pを持ち、Year 14までの3年間、受動的投資所得が総収入の90%（25%超）を超えていたため、Year 15の1月1日にS法人の選択が終了する。株主数100人はS法人の上限内であり、遺産財団は認められた株主で、寄附金はパススルーされて株主が控除できるため、いずれも終了事由にならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.80

questions.stem:
A corporation that has been an S corporation from its inception may
Be owned by a bankruptcy estate | Have both passive and nonpassive income

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
Grantor trusts, testamentary trusts, and bankruptcy estates are all permissible S corporation shareholders, while foreign trusts and charitable remainder trusts are not.

Note: A grantor trust is a type of living trust in which the person creating the trust (the grantor) remains the owner of the assets and property in the trust for both income and estate tax purposes.

Testamentary Trust is created in accordance with the instructions in a person's Last Will

"bankruptcy estate" describes the assets of the person who filed bankruptcy.

S corporations do not have restrictions on the type of income they can generate.
questions.explanationJa: グランター・トラスト、遺言信託、破産財団はいずれもS法人の株主になることが認められている（外国信託と慈善残余信託は認められない）。またS法人には、得られる所得の種類に制限はなく、受動的所得と非受動的所得の両方を持つことができる。したがって、破産財団による所有も、受動的・非受動的所得の両方を持つことも可能である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.81

questions.stem: Commerce Corp. elects S corporation status as of the beginning of Year 10. At the time of Commerce's election, it held a machine with a basis of $20,000 and a fair market value of $30,000. In March of Year 10, Commerce sells the machine for $35,000. What would be the amount subject to the built-in gains tax?
questions.explanation:
Although an S corporation is not subject to income taxes, Built-in gains [BIG] may apply if it was previously a C corporation. These taxes ensure that certain transactions do not escape taxation at the corporate level upon S corporation election.

Unrealized BIG applies when a C corporation elects S corporation status and the FMV of all assets held exceeds their basis (appreciated assets). The unrealized BIG represents the gain that would have been reported if the assets were sold before the S election. If the assets are sold within 5 years of electing S status, the S corporation pays the BIG tax, assessed at the highest corporate tax rate.

In this scenario, the machine had unrealized BIG of $10,000 ($30,000 FMV − $20,000 basis) at the time of conversion. The machine was sold within 5 years of the S election, so the S corporation will pay the BIG tax on $10,000 of gain.
questions.explanationJa: S法人は原則として法人税を納めないが、C法人からS法人に転換した場合はビルトイン・ゲイン（BIG）税がかかることがある。BIGは転換時点で資産の時価が簿価を上回っていた部分であり、転換後5年以内にその資産を売却すると、S法人は最高法人税率でBIG税を納める。機械の転換時の含み益は$30,000 − $20,000 = $10,000で、5年以内に売却したため、BIG税の対象は$10,000である。転換後に生じた$5,000の値上がりは対象外である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.82

questions.stem:
An individual has a 50% interest in a partnership, which has the following income and expense items:

Gross profit | $100,000
Selling, general, and administrative expenses | 60,000
Dividend income | 5,000
Capital gain | 3,000

What is the individual's qualified business income from the partnership?
questions.explanation:
Congress established a deduction for individuals, trusts, and estates that meet certain requirements and have qualified business income (QBI). Subject to limitations, the deduction is up to 20% of taxpayer QBI.

QBI comes from noncorporate U.S. businesses owned by the partnerships, S corporations, sole proprietorships. QBI is the operating income items. However, QBI does not include:

Reasonable compensation (wages)

Payments to a partner for services

Investment income (dividend income)

Capital gains/losses

Deductions allocable to investment income or capital gains/losses

In this scenario, the individual's QBI from the partnership is $20,000 (50% Allocation × [$100,000 Gross profit − $60,000 Selling, general, and administrative expenses]), which is the net of income items related to conducting the business (operating income).
questions.explanationJa: 適格事業所得（QBI）控除は、個人・信託・遺産財団に適格事業所得の最大20%を控除する制度である。QBIは事業の営業損益項目であり、合理的な報酬、パートナーへの役務の対価、配当などの投資所得、キャピタルゲイン・ロス、投資所得に対応する控除は含まない。この個人のQBIは、50% ×（売上総利益$100,000 − 販売費及び一般管理費$60,000）= $20,000である。配当$5,000とキャピタルゲイン$3,000は含めない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.83

questions.stem: The two equal shareholders of a C corporation are thinking of filing an election to have the company treated as an S corporation. Which of the following consequences is an advantage of this election?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The corporation's net operating loss carryovers from prior years are immediately deductible by the shareholders.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The shareholders of the S corporation will be taxed only on distributions from the corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The corporation's tax-free fringe benefits for the shareholders will be deductible by the corporation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The corporation's capital losses can be claimed on the tax returns of the shareholders.

questions.explanation: Capital losses, which are not deductible to a C corporation but may be carried back or carried forward to offset capital gains. But each S corporation shareholder has the ability to deduct up to $3,000 of their share of S corporation capital losses immediately, this is a unique benefit of S corporation status. Net capital loss or net operating loss carryforwards of the C corporation, however, would not be immediately deductible by the newly-formed S corporation's shareholders, but could be used to offset any built-in gains (BIG) tax that arises from the sale of appreciated assets during the recognition period. Fringe benefits are also deductible for a C corporation, so their deductibility would not be an advantage of making an S corporation election. S corporation shareholders are taxed on all income of the S corporation, regardless of whether it is distributed.
questions.explanationJa: C法人の資本損失は資本利得としか相殺できず、繰戻し・繰越しで処理する。これに対しS法人では、各株主が自分に配分されたS法人の資本損失を年$3,000まで即時に控除できるため、S法人選択の利点となる。C法人時代の純資本損失やNOLの繰越しは株主が即時に控除できるわけではなく、BIG税の相殺に使えるにとどまる。フリンジベネフィットはC法人でも損金算入でき、S法人の株主は分配の有無にかかわらずS法人の全所得に課税される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.84

questions.stem:
An individual taxpayer owns 100% of Markee, an S-Corporation, and has an initial basis of $10,000. This is the first year of Markee's operations. Additional items reported by Markee during the current year are:

Municipal bond interest | $10,000
Ordinary income | 3,400
Nondeductible entertainment expenses | 4,000
Shareholder distributions | 5,000

What was the taxpayer's basis in Markee at the end of the year?
questions.explanation:
Calculation of shareholder's basis in an S corporation

    Shareholder's beginning basis

  + Additional contributions

  + Percentage share of ordinary income and separately stated income, gains

  − Distributions from corporation (cash and property)

  − Percentage share of operating loss and separately stated deductions, losses

    Ending basis (never below Zero)

Note: Tax-exempt interest increases basis; nondeductible expenses decrease basis.
questions.explanationJa: S法人株主の簿価は、期首簿価に追加出資と所得・利得の持分を加え、分配と損失・控除の持分を差し引いて求め、ゼロを下回らない。非課税の地方債利息は簿価を増やし、損金不算入の交際費は簿価を減らす。期首簿価$10,000に地方債利息$10,000と通常所得$3,400を加え、分配$5,000と損金不算入の交際費$4,000を差し引くと、期末簿価は$14,400となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.85

questions.stem: Ignoring any limitations, a Section 199A qualified business income deduction may be claimed on which of the following tax returns?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any business tax return.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Individual tax returns.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pass-through entity tax returns.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Corporate tax returns.

questions.explanation: Subject to limitations, a deduction of up to 20% of qualified business income (QBI) is available to individuals, trusts, and estates. If eligible, the deduction is claimed on the tax return of the individual, trust, or estate that receives the QBI. In general, the deduction does not apply to income received from a C corporation.
questions.explanationJa: Section 199Aの適格事業所得（QBI）控除は、適格事業所得の最大20%を個人・信託・遺産財団に認める制度である。控除はQBIを受け取った個人・信託・遺産財団の申告で行い、パススルー事業体や法人の申告では行わない。原則としてC法人からの所得には適用されない。したがって、この控除を申告できるのは個人の申告書である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.86

questions.stem:
A taxpayer is the sole shareholder of Swallow, an S corporation. The taxpayer's adjusted basis in Swallow stock is $60,000 at the beginning of the year. During the year, Swallow reports the following income items:

Ordinary income | $30,000
Tax-exempt income | 5,000
Capital gains | 10,000

In addition, Swallow makes a nontaxable distribution to the taxpayer of $20,000 during the year. What is the taxpayer's adjusted basis in the Swallow stock at the end of the year?
questions.explanation:
All items of income, regardless of character, will increase basis in an S corporation. This includes tax-exempt income. Distributions reduce basis as a return of capital.

In this scenario, the taxpayer's ending basis in 100% of Swallow is $85,000, as shown below:

Beginning basis | $60,000
+ Ordinary income | 30,000
+ Tax-exempt income | 5,000
+ Capital gains | 10,000
− Distribution | (20,000)
Ending basis | $85,000
questions.explanationJa: S法人の簿価は、性質にかかわらずすべての所得項目で増え、非課税所得も含まれる。分配は資本の払戻しとして簿価を減らす。期首簿価$60,000に通常所得$30,000、非課税所得$5,000、キャピタルゲイン$10,000を加え、分配$20,000を差し引くと、期末簿価は$85,000となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.87

questions.stem: On January 1 of the first year of operation, an investor paid $10,000 for a 20% interest in Biga, an S corporation. During the same year, Biga earned $10,000 taxable income and $2,000 tax-exempt interest. Biga paid dividends totaling $1,000 to its shareholders during the same year. What is the investor's tax basis in the shares of Biga at the end of the year?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the investor's basis is $12,200, calculated as follows:

Beginning basis | $ 10,000
Share of ordinary income (10,000 × 20%) | 2,000
Share of tax-exempt interest (2,000 × 20%) | 400
Less share of distribution (1,000 × 20%) | (200)
Ending basis | $ 12,200
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.88

questions.stem: An S corporation is not permitted to take a deduction for

choices.label: A
choices.text: Compensation of officers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Interest paid to individuals who are not stockholders of the S corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Charitable contributions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Employee benefit programs established for individuals who are not stockholders of the S corporation.

questions.explanation:
An S corporation is permitted a deduction for items included in nonseparately calculated ordinary business net income/loss. Salaries paid to employees, whether or not they are shareholders, are ordinary business expenses ("Compensation of officers."). Interest expense paid to an unrelated party and employee benefit expenses are also ordinary business expenses ("Interest paid to individuals who are not stockholders of the S corpor…" / "Employee benefit programs established for individuals who are not sto…") and therefore are deductible for an S corporation.

Charitable contributions are separately stated due to AGI limitations at the taxpayer level. This item may be treated differently on individual shareholders' tax returns. For example, one shareholder may treat charitable contributions as an itemized deduction while another shareholder takes the standard deduction and thus cannot deduct contributions. Therefore, charitable contributions are not deducted at the entity level.
questions.explanationJa: S法人は、区分表示されない通常事業損益に含まれる項目を控除できる。株主であるかどうかにかかわらず従業員への給与は通常の事業費用であり、株主以外への支払利息や従業員福利制度の費用も同様に控除できる。一方、寄附金はAGIに基づく制限を株主段階で受け、株主ごとに扱いが異なりうる（項目別控除を選ぶ株主と標準控除を選ぶ株主がいる）ため、区分表示項目とされる。したがって寄附金は事業体段階では控除できない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.89

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct regarding the at-risk rules for shareholder losses in an S corporation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The at-risk rules depend on the S corporation's debt-to-equity ratio.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The at-risk rules vary based on the type of income reported by the S corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The at-risk rules apply at the shareholder level, not the corporate level.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The at-risk rules limit the S corporation's net operating loss carryover.

questions.explanation:
A shareholder's ability to deduct losses may be limited by basis, at-risk, and passive loss rules. At-risk rules were designed to prevent taxpayers from using shelters to deduct losses in excess of their economic risk.

For S corporation shareholders, the at-risk amount is generally the sum of the shareholder's investment in the entity (stock basis). The at-risk rules are applied at the shareholder level, not the entity level.
questions.explanationJa: 株主が損失を控除できるかどうかは、簿価、アットリスク、パッシブロスの各規定で制限されることがある。アットリスク規定は、経済的に負っているリスクを超える損失の控除を防ぐためのものである。S法人株主のアットリスク額は原則として事業体への投資額（株式簿価）であり、この規定は法人段階ではなく株主段階で適用される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.90

questions.stem: Monie, an individual taxpayer, owns 50% of Monie & Co, an S corporation. At the beginning of 20X4, Monie's basis in Monie & Co was $55,000. During 20X4, Monie & Co realized ordinary loss in the amount of $45,000 and a short-term capital loss of $15,000. Monie & Co made total distributions of $70,000 to its shareholders during this taxable year. What is Monie's resulting basis in Monie & Co after accounting for the above items?
questions.explanation: Because Monie is a 50% shareholder, the distribution amount is $35,000 (70,000 / 2 = 35,000). This $35,000 distribution decreases Monie's basis to $20,000. Monie's share of the loss items then decreases Monie's basis to zero but no lower, since basis cannot be negative.
questions.explanationJa: Monieは50%株主なので、分配の持分は$70,000 ÷ 2 = $35,000である。期首簿価$55,000から先に分配$35,000を差し引くと、簿価は$20,000となる。次に通常損失の持分$22,500と短期キャピタルロスの持分$7,500で簿価を減らすが、簿価はマイナスにならないため$0となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.91

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer, a 25% shareholder in an S corporation, had a stock basis of $10,000 at the beginning of the year. The corporation had ordinary income of $200,000 for the year. There were no separately stated items. The taxpayer received wages from the corporation of $25,000 and a distribution of $30,000. What was the taxpayer's basis in the stock at year end?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the taxpayer's beginning basis of $10,000 is increased for the pro rata share of income and decreased by the distribution. The ending basis is $30,000, as calculated below.

Beginning basis | $10,000
+ Share of income (25% × $200,000) | 50,000
− Distribution | (30,000)
= Ending basis | $30,000
questions.explanationJa: 株主の期首簿価$10,000は、通常所得の持分だけ増え、分配の分だけ減る。所得の持分は25% × $200,000 = $50,000、分配は$30,000である。期末簿価は$10,000 + $50,000 − $30,000 = $30,000となる。法人から受け取った給与$25,000は株主の給与所得であり、株式簿価には影響しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.92

questions.stem: On August 15, Year 1, Dryco Corp., a calendar-year S corporation, acquired 100% of the stock of an active C corporation. As a result of the acquisition, as of what date will Dryco's S election terminate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: January 1, Year 1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: August 15, Year 1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: December 31, Year 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Election will not terminate.

questions.explanation: One of the requirements for an S corporation election is that all shareholders be individuals or certain estates and trusts. Although the requirement excludes corporations as shareholders, there is nothing to prevent an S corporation from owning stock in a corporation.
questions.explanationJa: S法人の要件の一つは、株主がすべて個人または一定の遺産財団・信託であることである。この要件は法人がS法人の株主になることを禁じるものであり、S法人が他の法人の株式を所有することは禁じていない。したがってDryco Corp.がC法人の株式を100%取得しても、S法人の選択は終了しない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.93

questions.stem: Village Corp., a June 30 fiscal-year-end corporation, began business in Year 1. Village made a valid S Corporation election on September 5, Year 8, with the unanimous consent of its shareholders. The eligibility requirements for S status were met throughout Year 8. On what date did Village's S status become effective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: July 1, Year 8

choices.label: B
choices.text: September 5, Year 8

choices.label: C
choices.text: January 1, Year 9

choices.label: D
choices.text: July 1, Year 9

questions.explanation:
The election must be made within the first 2 1/2 months of the tax year (September 15 for a June 30 fiscal-year-end corporation) to be effective for the current year. Any election made after is effective at the start of the following tax year.

If a timely election is made retroactive to the start of the current year, all S corporation requirements must be met in the pre-election period, including unanimous shareholder consent. If the conditions are not met in the pre-election period, the election will be deferred to the start of following year.

Here, Village Corp. made the election on September 5, which is within the first 2 1/2 months of the tax year. Village met all S corporation requirements for the period and had unanimous consent. As a result, the election will go into effect on July 1, Year 8.
questions.explanationJa: S法人の選択を当年度から有効にするには、事業年度開始から2か月半以内（6月30日決算法人なら9月15日まで）に行う必要があり、それ以降の選択は翌事業年度の開始日から有効となる。当年度に遡って有効とするには、選択前の期間もS法人の要件（株主全員の同意を含む）を満たしていなければならない。Village Corp.は期限内の9月5日に選択し、要件と全員の同意も満たしていた。したがってS法人の地位はYear 8の7月1日から有効となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.94

questions.stem:
An S corporation had the following income and expenses:

Sales | $240,000
Rent expense | 25,000
Meals expense (all subject to 50% limitation) | 5,000
Interest income | 1,500
Contributions to qualifying charities | 600
Section 179 expense | 3,000
Depreciation expense | 1,800

What would be reported as ordinary income on the corporation's income tax return?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, due to statutory limitations at the shareholder level, the following are treated as separately stated items:

Interest income (required for shareholders' investment interest limitation)

Charitable contributions (subject to AGI limitations)

Section 179 expense (separate from depreciation expense and subject to annual dollar limitations).

The S corporation would report ordinary business income of $210,700: sales of $240,000 less the rent expense of $25,000, the depreciation expense of $1,800, and 50% of the $5,000 meals expense. While the meals expense is subject to a 50% limitation, the limitation is applied at the entity level and is not separately stated
questions.explanationJa: S法人では、株主段階の制限に関わる項目を区分表示する。受取利息は株主の投資利息制限に、寄附金はAGI制限に、Section 179費用は年間限度額にそれぞれ関わるため、いずれも区分表示項目となる。通常所得は、売上$240,000から賃借料$25,000、減価償却費$1,800、交際費$5,000の50%である$2,500を差し引いた$210,700となる。交際費の50%制限は事業体段階で適用され、区分表示はしない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.95

questions.stem: Packer Corp., an accrual-basis, calendar-year S corporation, has been an S corporation since its inception. Starr was a 50% shareholder in Packer throughout the current year and had a $10,000 tax basis in Packer stock on January 1. During the current year, Packer had a $1,000 net business loss and made an $8,000 cash distribution to each shareholder. What amount of the distribution was includible in Starr's gross income?
questions.explanation: Normally cash distributions are non-taxable to the extent of a shareholder's basis in an S corporation. Starr's basis was decreased from $10,000 to $2,000 as a result of the $8,000 distribution. After the distribution is accounted for, Starr's basis is reduced by another $500, to $1,500, as a result of Starr's 50% share of Packer's loss.
questions.explanationJa: S法人からの現金分配は、株主の簿価の範囲内であれば課税されない。Starrの簿価$10,000は$8,000の分配によって$2,000に減る。分配を反映した後、事業損失$1,000の50%である$500で簿価はさらに$1,500に減る。分配は簿価の範囲内なので、総所得に含める額は$0である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.96

questions.stem: An S corporation is owned equally by A and B, whose respective stock bases at the beginning of the year are $12,000 and $13,000. During the year, the corporation had $100,000 in ordinary business income and $5,000 in tax-exempt income. The corporation distributed $50,000 to each shareholder for the year. What is owner B's stock basis at year end?
questions.explanation:
In this scenario, the ending stock basis for B's 50% interest is $15,500, calculated as follows:

A's basis | B's basis
Beginning balance | $12,000 | $13,000
Ordinary income (50% share) | 50,000 | 50,000
Tax-exempt income (50% share) | 2,500 | 2,500
Distribution | (50,000) | (50,000)
Ending basis | $14,500 | $15,500
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Corporate Taxation Q.97

questions.stem: In calculating the tax of a corporation for a short period, which of the following processes is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Divide current-year income by prior-year income, then multiply the result by prior-year tax.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compute tax on short-period income, then multiply the result by 12 divided by the number of months in the short period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Determine the average taxable income for the past three years, then multiply the result by the number of months in the short period divided by 12.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Annualize income and calculate the tax on annualized income, then multiply the computed tax by the number of months in the short period divided by 12.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §443(b)(1), when a short period return is required because of a change in annual accounting period, taxable income for the short period is annualized: it is multiplied by 12 and divided by the number of months in the short period. Tax is computed on the annualized income, and the resulting tax is then multiplied by the number of months in the short period divided by 12.

Dividing current-year income by prior-year income and applying the ratio to prior-year tax is not a method found in the Code.
Computing tax on the short-period income and then multiplying by 12/months reverses the process and would overstate the tax.
Averaging three years of income is not the annualization method.
questions.explanationJa:
会計期間の変更により短期間の申告が必要な場合、短期間の課税所得を年換算（×12÷短期間の月数）し、その年換算所得に対して税額を計算し、その税額に（短期間の月数÷12）を掛けて短期間の税額とする（IRC §443(b)(1)）。
前年所得との比率を前年税額に掛ける方法や、過去3年平均を使う方法は規定に無い。短期間所得の税額に12/月数を掛ける方法は順序が逆で、税額を過大にする。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.8 (AICPA No. 9848)

questions.stem: Simon, a C corporation, had a deficit in accumulated earnings and profits of $50,000 at the beginning of the year and had current earnings and profits of $10,000. At year end, Simon paid a dividend of $15,000 to its sole shareholder. What amount of the dividend is reported as income?
questions.explanation:
A distribution from a C corporation is a dividend to the extent of earnings and profits (IRC §316(a)). A distribution is first treated as made out of current E&P, computed at year end without regard to any deficit in accumulated E&P. Accumulated E&P is used only after current E&P is exhausted, and a deficit in accumulated E&P does not reduce current E&P.

Dividend from current E&P = $10,000
Remaining distribution = $15,000 - $10,000 = $5,000 (return of capital, then capital gain if it exceeds stock basis)
Dividend income = $10,000

The $0 amount incorrectly nets the accumulated deficit against current E&P.
The $5,000 amount is the portion of the distribution in excess of current E&P, which is not a dividend.
The $15,000 amount treats the entire distribution as a dividend even though total E&P available is only $10,000.
questions.explanationJa:
C法人の分配は、E&P（利益積立金）の範囲内で配当となる（IRC §316(a)）。まず当期E&P（期末時点で算定し、累積E&Pの欠損とは相殺しない）から分配されたものとし、当期E&Pを使い切った後に累積E&Pが充当される。
当期E&P $10,000 → 配当 $10,000。残り $5,000 は資本の払戻し（株式の取得価額を超えれば譲渡益）。
$0 は累積欠損を当期E&Pと相殺しており誤り。$5,000 は当期E&Pを超える部分で配当ではない。$15,000 は全額を配当としている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.19 (AICPA No. 9959)

questions.stem: Stone owns 100% of an S corporation and materially participates in its operations. The stock basis at the beginning of the year is $5,000. During the year, the corporation makes a distribution of $3,500 and passes through a loss from operations of $2,000 for the year. What loss can Stone deduct on Stone's personal tax return?
questions.explanation:
An S corporation shareholder's stock basis is adjusted in this order: increased by income items, decreased by distributions, then decreased by nondeductible expenses and losses (IRC §1368(d), Treas. Reg. §1.1367-1(f)). A shareholder may deduct losses only to the extent of stock basis (plus debt basis) remaining after these adjustments (IRC §1366(d)(1)).

Beginning stock basis = $5,000
Less distribution = ($3,500)
Basis available for loss = $1,500
Deductible loss = lesser of $2,000 loss or $1,500 basis = $1,500 (the remaining $500 is suspended)

The $0 amount ignores the basis remaining after the distribution.
The $2,000 amount applies the loss before the distribution, which reverses the required ordering.
The $5,500 amount adds the distribution to the loss; a distribution is not a deductible loss.
questions.explanationJa:
S法人株主の株式取得価額（stock basis）は、①所得項目で増額 → ②分配で減額 → ③損失で減額、の順で調整し、損失は残った basis の範囲内でのみ控除できる（IRC §1366(d)(1)、§1368(d)）。
期首 $5,000 − 分配 $3,500 = $1,500 → 損失 $2,000 のうち控除できるのは $1,500（残り $500 は繰越）。
$0 は分配後に残る basis を無視している。$2,000 は分配より先に損失を充てており順序が逆。$5,500 は分配を損失に加えているが、分配は損失ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.34 (AICPA No. 9974)

questions.stem: On January 1 of the current year, Locke Corp., an accrual-basis calendar-year C corporation, had $30,000 in accumulated earnings and profits. For the current year, Locke had current earnings and profits of $20,000, and made two $40,000 cash distributions to its shareholders, one in April and one in September. What amount of the distributions is classified as dividend income to Locke's shareholders?
questions.explanation:
Distributions are dividends to the extent of E&P (IRC §316). Current E&P is allocated pro rata to all distributions made during the year. Accumulated E&P is then allocated to distributions in chronological order (Treas. Reg. §1.316-2(b), (c)).

Current E&P allocated to each distribution = $20,000 x ($40,000 / $80,000) = $10,000
April distribution: $10,000 current + $30,000 accumulated = $40,000 dividend
September distribution: $10,000 current + $0 accumulated (exhausted) = $10,000 dividend
Total dividend income = $40,000 + $10,000 = $50,000

The $0 amount ignores both current and accumulated E&P.
The $20,000 amount counts only current E&P and ignores accumulated E&P.
The $80,000 amount treats the entire distributions as dividends although total E&P is only $50,000.
questions.explanationJa:
分配は E&P の範囲内で配当となる（IRC §316）。当期E&Pは全分配に分配額の比で按分し、累積E&Pは日付の早い分配から順に充当する（Treas. Reg. §1.316-2）。
当期E&Pの按分 = $20,000 × 1/2 = 各 $10,000。4月分 = $10,000 + 累積 $30,000 = $40,000、9月分 = $10,000 + 累積 $0 = $10,000、配当合計 $50,000。
$0 は E&P を無視している。$20,000 は当期E&Pのみで累積E&Pを考慮していない。$80,000 は分配全額を配当としているが、E&Pの合計は $50,000 しかない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.1 (AICPA No. 89801)

questions.stem: For year 2, Quest Corp., an accrual-basis calendar-year C corporation, had an $8,000 unexpired charitable contribution carryover from year 1. Quest's year 2 taxable income before the deduction for charitable contributions was $200,000. On December 12, year 2, Quest's board of directors authorized a $15,000 cash contribution to a qualified charity, which was made on January 6, year 3. What is the maximum allowable deduction that Quest may take as a charitable contribution on its year 2 income tax return?
questions.explanation:
A corporation's charitable contribution deduction is limited to 10% of taxable income computed without the charitable deduction, the dividends-received deduction, NOL carrybacks, and capital loss carrybacks (IRC §170(b)(2)). An accrual-basis corporation may deduct a contribution authorized by its board during the year if it is paid within 3½ months after year end (IRC §170(a)(2)); the January 6, year 3 payment qualifies. Unused carryovers from prior years are added to the current-year contributions, subject to the same limit.

10% limit = $200,000 x 10% = $20,000
